articles.title: Dianna Russini Addresses Her Absence in New Show Premiere 7 Months After Mike Vrabel Photo Scandal
articles.summary: Russini will host the show every Wednesday on BetUS TV
articles.body:
Dianna Russini talked about her newfound "perspective" on the first episode of her show, The Russini Report, on Wednesday, Nov. 11

The show marks Russini's return to sports media after resigning from The Athletic in April, following her photo scandal with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel

Russini told PEOPLE in her first interview since the scandal that she's "not scared to get back in because I know the people that I cover are welcoming me back with open arms"

Dianna Russini made her official return to sports media with the debut episode of her new show, The Russini Report.

On the first episode of her new BetUS TV show on Wednesday, Nov. 11, Russini, 43, began the show with a "personal note" touching on her months away.

"Over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life and my priorities and the person that I want to be moving forward, and being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys and being truly present, it gave me so much perspective that I didn't even know I needed," Russini said.

The show's premiere comes seven months after she resigned from The Athletic due to paparazzi photos of her and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel embracing and holding hands at an Arizona hotel that were published by Page Six, along with photos of the pair in an N.Y.C. bar in 2020 and renting a boat in Tennessee in 2021.

Russini told PEOPLE in an exclusive interview two days before the premiere that the show is "about everything I know that's going on in the NFL, along with a lot of my opinions," describing the latter as "something I wasn't really allowed to do before."

The show's premiere did not go off without a hitch, though, and technical difficulties delayed the start by close to 45 minutes. Bet US said the "record-breaking audience" broke the livestream. Once on air, Russini talked about the NFL trade deadline and talked with SiriusXM host Damon Amendolara, Philadelphia radio host Spike Eskin and former NFL coach Bill Parcels.

Speaking to PEOPLE ahead of the premiere, Russini said she was "very excited" for this new chapter, but the photo scandal was "a nightmare" for her. "The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking."

Both Russini and her husband , Kevin Goldschmidt, both deleted their X accounts following the scandal. "The lies became so out of control," Russini claimed.

"This was a runaway train, and there was nothing I could do to stop it. Once we realized nothing was going to stop this, it became unhealthy for us to read it because it wasn't helping us heal. It was piling on and adding to what we were already dealing with."

Yet, she said she felt a lot of support from people around the NFL. "The absolute best part of this situation has been the loyalty the NFL has shown me. They checked in with me almost daily while I wasn't working to make sure that I was staying connected to football, to check on me as a person and to just see how I was doing," Russini told PEOPLE.

She recalled, "I felt like players were texting and calling me to say, 'Get back to work, it's time,' and added, "I think it's pretty poetic that here I was all these years telling the story about these players going through adversity, and then they became sort of the people that I was learning from during this."

articles.title: Former Giants coach defends star player Malik Nabers against character questions from broadcast analyst
articles.summary: Wink Martindale says someone may have put criticism in Greg Olsen's ear about Malik Nabers, suggesting motives tied to the Giants star's contract.
articles.body: When his character came into question, Giants star wideout Malik Nabers took to social media to take on former player and TV analyst Greg Olsen, who criticized the receiver’s sideline demeanor during Sunday's broadcast. One former New York Giants coach is running to Nabers' defense. Ex-Giants defensive coordinator Wink Martindale, who had a messy split with the team in 2024, harbors no bad blood toward the receiver and spoke up to defend Nabers against Olsen's critique. "I'm with Malik on this. Somebody put that in his ear, whether it's to keep his contract down for the next year when they want to extend him or whatever it is, I don't know. But just keep playing," Martindale said, appearing on Giants insider Pat Leonard's "Talkin' Ball" podcast. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I love the kid. I love his competitiveness." During the Giants' visit to Philadelphia on Sunday, Olsen and boothmate Joe Davis kept pointing to Nabers' "negative" body language on the sideline. They also called him out for pouting after a Giants drive finished with an Isaiah Likely touchdown. "His body language has been terrible today," Davis said. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS STAR DEFENSIVE LINEMAN CHRIS JONES CAUGHT IN SCREAMING MATCH WITH COACHES ON SIDELINES Olsen proved more frustrated with Nabers. "I have played with a lot of really good wide receivers, a lot [of] really good players. There's never been a great wide receiver who hasn't demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory. But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That's great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He is a talented, young, really good player. You've just got to keep it in check." Martindale added, "Think about all the great players that John Harbaugh's coached. Does he get blown up more because it's in New York? Of course it does. But it's nothing new for John." Martindale knows a thing or two about friction inside New York's building. Following months of simmering tension during the 2023 season, his Giants tenure imploded in January 2024 after head coach Brian Daboll fired Martindale’s trusted defensive assistants. Martindale reportedly cursed out Daboll, stormed out, and mutually parted ways. Despite showing visible frustration during the Giants' 19-11 win in Philadelphia, where he had five catches for 43 yards after four straight 100-yard games, Nabers' commitment was never questioned by his locker room. Giants players publicly defended him as a "good teammate, " with running back Cam Skattebo noting that Nabers' sideline annoyance when lacking targets simply reflects a competitive edge teammates "love to see." articles.title: Daniel Jones 'Not Happy' Colts Traded Keenan Allen, Josh Downs and More In NFL Deadline Fire Sale
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are going to look much different when they take the field for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins than they did at the start of the season after a number of trades, and quarterback Daniel Jones isn't thrilled about the situation.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are going to look much different when they take the field for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins than they did at the start of the season after a number of trades, and quarterback Daniel Jones isn't thrilled about the situation.

"I mean, honestly, you're not not happy to see it, right?" Jones told reporters (h/t Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk). "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and—but like I said, it's outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming into those spots, and we'll be ready to go."

Indianapolis traded wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, as well as defensive lineman DeForest Buckner and offensive lineman Quenton Nelson. Allen and Downs were two of Jones' top targets in the aerial attack, while Nelson was a key part in the protection up front.

Yet the Colts didn't end up trading running back Jonathan Taylor despite plenty of speculation they would, so Jones can at least still rely on his backfield mate and one of the best playmakers in the league to help lead the offense.

It has been a season to forget in Indianapolis, as it fell to 2-7 with Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Jones has struggled as well with six touchdown passes to 10 interceptions after largely playing well last season with 19 touchdown passes to just eight interceptions.

Losing the team's best offensive lineman and two of its top wide receivers won't make life easier for Jones, so it would be anything but a surprise if he continues to struggle from a statistical standpoint.

The Colts are in rebuilding mode at this point, but the immediate future doesn't look great for the quarterback or his teammates.

articles.title: “Just adore him and I think he is the greatest”: How Jason and Travis Kelce turned two Chiefs fans' unusual requests into special memories with heartfelt gestures
articles.summary: An autograph from an NFL star can become a lifelong memory. For two Kansas City Chiefs fans, that memory came in an unusual way.
articles.body: An autograph from an NFL star can become a lifelong memory. For two Kansas City Chiefs fans, that memory came in an unusual way. Jason and Travis Kelce each signed a fan's prosthetic leg during separate Chiefs games, turning two unexpected requests into memorable moments. While Jason's interaction happened in October 2024, Travis followed a year later, giving another supporter a reason to remember her night at Arrowhead Stadium.The two incidents also showed a different side of the Kelce brothers. Beyond their NFL achievements, both took time to connect with supporters who wanted something more personal than a photograph or a signed football.Jason Kelce and the ESPN crew answered Samantha Secord's unusual requestThe first incident took place on October 7, 2024, when the Chiefs hosted the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football. Samantha Secord, a Chiefs season-ticket holder from Omaha, travelled more than 184 miles to watch her team. This time, she had a special request: she wanted Jason Kelce to sign her prosthetic leg.Secord and her friends tried to get the ESPN crew's attention during the broadcast. Their efforts eventually worked when Scott Van Pelt noticed them and helped bring the leg to the crew. Jason and the other ESPN personalities signed it during a commercial break.Speaking to KCTV5 on October 10, 2024, Secord described the experience as "kind of mind-blowing." However, she still had one autograph in mind."My favorite player is Travis Kelce. I just adore him, and I think he is the greatest," she told KCTV5. "He is the one that I am absolutely looking forward to signing my leg."Her request carried a personal meaning. Secord lost her leg after a 2022 UTV accident that injured the lower half of her body. She also explained that watching Travis play and following his community work helped her during recovery. Travis Kelce signed another fan's prosthetic leg after reaching 100 touchdownsA year later, on October 27, 2025, Travis had his own memorable interaction with a Chiefs supporter. Kansas City defeated the Washington Commanders 28-7, and Kelce reached 100 career touchdown receptions, becoming only the fourth tight end in NFL history to achieve the milestone.After the game, a different female fan caught his attention by raising her prosthetic leg towards him. People around her helped pass it to the tight end, who signed it as the crowd cheered. ESPN shared the interaction on its TikTok page.The gesture came during a night when Kelce had plenty of reasons to celebrate. Speaking to Scott Van Pelt during ESPN's postgame interview, he joked about his longevity."I'm just the old lucky dog that's still able to do this thing," Kelce said.Patrick Mahomes also praised his longtime teammate after the victory, calling him the "true Chiefs Chief." Head coach Andy Reid highlighted Kelce's energy and continued contribution to Kansas City.The two incidents involved different fans, but they shared a similar moment of connection. articles.title: Struggling Colts QB Daniel Jones admits he's 'not happy' watching Indy's front office strip away teammates
articles.summary: Daniel Jones admitted he's frustrated after the Colts dealt Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, and Josh Downs in a two-week sell-off.
articles.body: The captain of the sinking 2-7 Colts ship is not happy. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones admitted he is frustrated watching the front office gut his supporting cast. Before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline passed, acting GM Ed Dodds traded away guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs over two weeks. Jones, 29, made his displeasure clear when facing reporters on Wednesday. "I mean, honestly, you’re not happy to see it, right?" Jones said. "You’re a player, and you’re going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you’re not happy to see a lot of those decisions, but like I said, it’s outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we’ll be ready to go." Jones is stuck throwing to backups, though his own play led to the teardown. Had DJ delivered, Indy would be buying instead of selling. Through nine games, the $88 million quarterback has six touchdown passes, 10 interceptions and a dismal 68.9 passer rating. articles.title: NFL midseason grades: 2 teams go from Super Bowl hopes to Fs, while overachieving Giants, Browns receive high praise
articles.summary: Yahoo Sports NFL analysts Frank Schwab and Eric Edholm evaluate all 32 teams at the halfway mark of the 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
AFC East: Patriots | Bills | Dolphins | Jets AFC North: Steelers | Ravens | Bengals | Browns AFC South: Colts | Jaguars | Texans | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chargers | Chiefs | Raiders

NFC East: Eagles | Cowboys | Commanders | Giants NFC North: Packers | Lions | Bears | Vikings NFC South: Buccaneers | Panthers | Falcons | Saints NFC West: Seahawks | Rams | 49ers | Cardinals

After 136 games this NFL season, the New York Giants and Washington Commanders will kick off the second half of this season Thursday night.

Who has impressed us most? Who has been a letdown? Following up their trade deadline grades , Yahoo Sports' Frank Schwab and Eric Edholm had enough in the tank to give their first-half assessment of all 32 teams. Here are their grades, with Schwab critiquing the AFC and Edholm the NFC:

It's hard to have a much better first half of the season. The Bills are in pole position for the first seed in the AFC with just one loss, Josh Allen is having another MVP-level season and they made a nice addition at the trade deadline with safety Amani Hooker . The only reason the grade was lowered a bit was the disappointing start for the defense, which could be a problem in January.

Malik Willis' landing on injured reserve will make things even tougher for at least a few weeks. But everyone knew the Dolphins would be bad this season, and yet they have battled hard for first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Some young players, like rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, have had good moments. Miami's record is bad, but the first half has actually been somewhat encouraging.

The Patriots have a great win over the Bills but ugly losses to the Seahawks, Jaguars and Packers. Drake Maye has had some great games and some miserable ones, which mirrors the Patriots as a whole. Overall, it has been a disappointing follow-up to their AFC championship season. There's still hope for a better second half.

The season started well, with a win at Tennessee. The Jets are 1-7 since then. At least the Jets have three top-13 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft if the season ended today, and 2026 second overall pick David Bailey looks like a big hit. Head coach Aaron Glenn is very unlikely to be back next season, but that allows the Jets to start anew with a treasure trove of picks.

The Bengals had two assignments this season: Keep Joe Burrow upright and field a competent defense. They've done both, and are in great position to win the AFC North and also get Burrow his first MVP. Some more activity at the trade deadline might have been nice but the Bengals dealt for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II in the offseason and he has had a huge impact.

It's fine to be skeptical of the Steelers' staying power, but they are winning games and also getting better. Head coach Mike McCarthy is leaning on the run game and it's working. Pittsburgh's defense is aging but has played well lately. The Steelers have a win over the Bengals and a record that is good as anyone could have expected at this point.

Give head coach Todd Monken credit for managing a bad quarterback situation and still getting the Browns to a winning record. The bad news is those wins will hurt their quest to fix their QB problem in the 2027 NFL Draft. For now it's a team that is winning games with an exciting young cast, including rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. The future is bright, as long as the Browns figure out QB soon.

The failing grade here isn't all Baltimore's fault. When a future Hall of Fame quarterback plays only four games because of injuries, there's not much you can do. But it's still a team that was in a Super Bowl window and now the season seems over with Lamar Jackson on injured reserve. And it's not all the offense: Jesse Minter's defense has allowed 104 points in its last three games.

The Jaguars have looked very good in the first half of the season and added a lot at the trade deadline . Their two losses came on a second-half fade at Denver and a field goal on the final play against Houston. The Jags lead the NFL in point differential and are first in DVOA. The Jaguars have never made a Super Bowl, but that's a realistic goal this season.

The Texans started 0-4 and also blew a game as a big favorite against the Giants. There's no way a team this talented should have five losses at the midway point, especially with quarterback C.J. Stroud playing his best ball since his rookie season. The Texans could still rally and make the playoffs but with a defense playing far below expectations, this is far less than Houston expected.

The Titans are still rebuilding, but you'd like to see more progress given a new head coach and all the money Tennessee spent in free agency ($333.9 million, most in the NFL). The Titans continue to be one of the worst teams in the NFL and there are still major questions about Cam Ward. They are lucky they beat a collapsing Colts team, or else we'd be hearing 0-17 questions.

The Colts didn't look terrible when they took the Chiefs to overtime in Week 2. But things have fallen apart since then. They fired general manager Chris Ballard and traded several key pieces, but weirdly hung onto running back Jonathan Taylor . Daniel Jones has been awful, and now the Colts know they have to start over at QB. Head coach Shane Steichen will surely get fired, whether it's during the season or after. The first half was so bad it will set the franchise back for years. It doesn't even have next year's first-round draft pick; that's off to the Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade. Yikes.

The questions about whether the Chiefs' dynasty is over seem to have been answered. Maybe this isn't a vintage Chiefs team, but their only losses were on the road against tough opponents (Seahawks, Broncos). They've reinvented themselves with free-agent addition Kenneth Walker III now carrying the offense. It has been a nice rebound from a weird 6-11 season.

The Broncos are 7-2 with perhaps the best set of quality wins in the NFL: Jaguars, Rams, Seahawks and Chiefs. And yet, the idea that they're just getting by with an inordinate number of close wins (they barely beat the Chargers, let's not forget) is hard to shake. Is Denver a Super Bowl contender? Perhaps. Are they the NFL's biggest regression candidate? Also possible. For now, it's hard to argue with that record.

The Raiders are more competitive than in years past. And the Kirk Cousins trade shows that their front office finally seems to have a progressive plan to rebuild. But there are some concerning things, like a defense that ranks last in the NFL. We'll find out more in the second half of the season as Fernando Mendoza takes over at quarterback. The first half was promising, but also a reminder that this team is not yet a playoff contender.

It's hard to remember a team that was more disappointing. The Chargers had back-to-back 11-win seasons and looked stronger entering this season with improved health on the offensive line. Instead, they've been the worst team in football. Justin Herbert has been one of the worst quarterbacks in football. This collapse makes no sense. They deserve the lowest first-half grade in the NFL in many years. It has been that bad.

Record-wise, the Giants are off to a fantastic start, perhaps even above the rosiest-glasses fan's expectations in John Harbaugh's first season as head coach. It's even more impressive considering the season-ending injuries to stalwarts such as Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns and Tremaine Edmunds. The Giants are far from perfect, and it's clear they're taking advantage of a weakened NFC East field this season. But it's also hard to gripe too much with the early results with J.J. McCarthy taking over. The Giants' close-game toughness is undeniable, even if their ceiling this season feels moderately low for a first-place club.

We knew the Cowboys had a good offense coming into the season, and Dallas has scored 27-plus points in six games, but that unit hasn't been good enough to compensate for a defense that continues to struggle. They're only marginally better on that side of the ball in a few respects compared to 2025, and even marginally worse than last year in a few areas. The Cowboys still have a shot at the division title, but they'll need George Pickens and the defense to improve significantly.

It has been another rough season in Washington, with injuries blighting the operation, starting back in training camp when Laremy Tunsil went down. Look no further than Jayden Daniels missing two games with a left elbow injury, plus Terry McLaurin and others landing on injured reserve. It has been a tough coaching season, too, with Dan Quinn's feet put to the fire for late-game crumbling in multiple outings and a blowout loss to the Colts. Other than shocking the Seahawks at home, there hasn't been much to get excited about.

Even by the most pessimistic expectations, the Eagles' season has been a disaster. Two narrow wins were followed by seven brutal losses. Jalen Hurts being diagnosed with blood clots was the next catastrophic development, which has put his football future (and future in Philadelphia) in doubt. Hurts' replacements have struggled, which shouldn't be stunning. The Eagles' defense also turning into a sub-par unit has been among the bigger disappointments. If there's a silver lining, it's that general manager Howie Roseman procured major draft-pick compensation for Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis . That's also a reflection on how the season has gone.

The Bears have won four straight and are very much in the Super Bowl mix now. The trade for Jeffery Simmons has only raised the ceiling for the team, even if there are still questions about its defense. The offense also has to get back to running the ball better, which has been a problem with Kyle Monangai missing a chunk of games. Yet head coach Ben Johnson has found ways to put up points and has given quarterback Caleb Williams the reins. It hasn't always been pretty, and the home stretch will be grueling with Chicago facing one of the toughest remaining schedules and the division providing incredibly tough competition. The Bears, however, are for real, even going 2-1 with Williams out of the starting lineup with a hamstring injury.

A slow start, compounded by some notable player absences, put this team in an early hole. But the Packers have won five of six games since the disastrous home loss to the Falcons, and Jordan Love has entered the MVP discussion with his recent hot run. He has arguably the best top pair of receivers in the league right now with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. They'll have to keep flying without Josh Jacobs, who is out for an unclear amount of time (broken finger). Green Bay's defense has overachieved in spite of injuries, forcing multiple turnovers for six straight games, and Micah Parsons is on his way back. The arrow points up in a big way.

The Lions are on a four-game win streak, leveling up after a tepid start to the season where they were a few snaps away from an 0-4 record. Their defense, which has held four straight opponents to 21 or fewer points, has been inspiring. Linebacker Jack Campbell's injury, minimal help at the trade deadline (safety Andre Cisco) and the murky status of Kerby Joseph cap the optimism a bit. With Offensive Player of the Year candidate Jahmyr Gibbs leading the way, the Lions' offense can carry them most games. But Detroit finishes with some tough opponents, plus four of the final six games coming on the road.

Brian Flores' defense has been a terrific unit this season, keeping the Vikings in virtually every game. But what became obvious in the home loss to the Bills was that something needed to be done at quarterback. Kyler Murray hasn't played well on the whole, and replacement Carson Wentz was downright bad against Buffalo. That's why the Kirk Cousins trade feels like a potential season saver. The past two losses proved that even a Super Bowl-caliber D needs offensive help. If Cousins can meld back in and lift this unit up, the Vikings could be a problem, but they have to do it vs. the league's best teams.

Coming off a division title despite a losing record last season, the Panthers have unfortunately carried over their inconsistencies from a year ago, with a 1-2 start, two straight victories, and then three straight losses. And yes, they're somehow still in first place in the division. Even in a lower-bar division, it's hard to throw too many roses in their direction. Bryce Young and the Panthers' offense are functional, but there are still too many defensive issues — after big offseason acquisitions — to assume they'll work through them.

The Bucs have shown signs of life following their 0-4 start, with Todd Bowles' defense and Bucky Irving's running keeping them in games. Baker Mayfield's struggles and a thumb injury that cost him three games (and forced undrafted Jalon Daniels into the lineup) have held the offense back, and the offseason loss of Mike Evans can't be overstated. All six of their losses have been by one score, and their point differential (plus-24) is by far the best in the division. Still, this has been a disappointing first half. The league's easiest remaining schedule keeps the lights on for now in Tampa.

They started 0-2 amid QB problems, and then Michael Penix Jr. delivered five straight solid performances, helping kick-start the offense. Even with that, the Falcons still dropped close games to the Ravens and Bears, and things have turned even more sour since beating the 49ers. The Falcons looked borderline uncompetitive in their past two games, outscored 50-17. The young core and offensive weapons are exciting, but the Falcons remain a muddled lot.

Ask yourself: What is this team's strength? What is its identity? Neither has been easy to discern this season. Even more frustrating is the Saints' 1-3 mark at the Superdome. They still have five division games remaining, and the NFC South remains wide open, with every team two or more games under .500. But Tyler Shough will need to continue developing, and the defense will need to keep building on its incremental improvements of late.

Injuries have continued sinking their teeth into the roster, but the 49ers keep winning games. Head coach Kyle Shanahan deserves a ton of credit for how this team has played, starting with a season-opening blowout of the Rams in Australia. Even with the disappointing loss to the Falcons, there hasn't been much to complain about, pacing a division billed as one of the league's finest. The Niners will have to continue winning against a road-heavy schedule of mostly contending teams down the stretch and cross their fingers for better injury luck, but there is championship-level DNA on this roster.

They were hailed as arguably the best team in football in August, and one local writer infamously predicted a 17-0 regular-season mark. That took all of four quarters to turn to ashes, and injuries have damaged this roster, especially at wide receiver . With Myles Garrett back and Aaron Donald still thriving, L.A.'s defense might have to carry the team for a stretch. That unit, hardly dominant, has been better since the Buffalo loss. The Rams are on track after a tough start, but they're still searching for a signature win.

Multiple injuries for Sam Darnold, plus his own poor play (nine INTs in his past six games) have hurt the offense. The Seahawks also have struggled to run the ball consistently without Kenneth Walker III, especially as rookie running back Jadarian Price missed a chunk of the season on IR. That has made them far too dependent on Jaxon Smith-Njigba to move the ball, amazing as he is. Defensively, the Seahawks are still strong, but they've allowed as many 30-point games in half a season as they did in all of 2025.

Beating the Rams and Cowboys on the road deserves praise, and the Cardinals' 3-3 road mark has kept the season from being a disaster. But the offense continues to largely struggle outside of a few promising spurts. They're about to start their third QB in Carson Beck , and the decision to draft Jeremiyah Love hasn't yet paid off. Defensively, they've been inconsistent at best, allowing six opponents to cross the 30-point threshold, including in all three home games. Expectations were low entering the season, and Arizona is playing to about that level.

articles.title: Broncos' deal for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley falls through after NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: No reason was provided for the trade getting spiked.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos appeared to fill an immediate need with a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. That deal is no longer happening.

Denver announced in a statement late Wednesday night that the deal, which would have seen the Chargers receive a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick , was no longer happening. No reason was provided.

"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized. We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward."

The development means Henley will remain with the Chargers, the only winless team in the NFL at 0-8. The deal was going to be a rental for the Broncos as Henley is a pending free agent, but the former third-round draft pick will now spend the remainder of the final year of his rookie contract in Los Angeles.

Henley has a salary of $3.7 million this season, per OverTheCap .

The Broncos, who have won five straight games, approached Tuesday's trade deadline in need of additional depth at linebacker and appeared to get that in the 27-year-old Henley, who leads the Chargers with 51 combined tackles as well as two passes defended, a forced fumble, an interception and a half sack in eight games this season.

Denver's defense ranks 10th in points allowed and 26th in total yards, while also playing more snaps than any unit in the NFL at 648. Veteran inside linebacker Alex Singleton has played 647 of those, making him the most-used defensive player in the league, and fellow inside linebacker Justin Strnad isn't far behind him at 529 snaps.

Henley would have helped give that pair some rest as a rotational option, but the Broncos will have to figure that situation out without the help of the trade deadline.

articles.title: Chiefs' Harrison Butker problem takes another turn as Andy Reid makes a crucial call before Falcons showdown
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are giving Harrison Butker another opportunity despite his disappointing form, and Andy Reid's latest decision has done little to
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are giving Harrison Butker another opportunity despite his disappointing form, and Andy Reid's latest decision has done little to calm frustrated fans. With the Atlanta Falcons coming up in Week 10, the Chiefs head coach has confirmed that Butker will remain the team's starting kicker. The call is notable because Kansas City already has another experienced option in Justin Tucker. But rather than make an immediate change, Reid is prepared to give Butker more time, even as his missed kicks continue to raise questions about the team's kicking situation.Andy Reid backs Harrison Butker despite his poor numbersButker's struggles have become increasingly difficult for Kansas City to overlook. The kicker has failed to deliver the consistency expected from him, with costly misses putting extra pressure on the team during important moments.His problems became more noticeable after the Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7, when he missed two field goal attempts. Kansas City then faced the Denver Broncos in Week 8, and Butker missed a 54-yard attempt late in the game. The miss added to the growing frustration around his performances.Although the Chiefs responded with a convincing 35-12 victory over the New York Jets in Week 9, Butker did not completely put his kicking problems behind him. He missed his only field goal attempt in that game, while his season conversion rate stood at just 63.2%.That figure is a major concern for a team that often finds itself in close games, where a reliable kicker can make a significant difference. Reid, however, has chosen to stick with the player he knows rather than make a change before the Falcons game.Speaking about his decision, the Chiefs coach said, “I’m going to stick with Butker,” making his position clear ahead of Sunday's contest.The decision also followed Reid's earlier comments after the Jets win, when he said he would review the situation before reaching a conclusion. He has now completed that review, and Butker has retained his starting role.Justin Tucker's arrival makes the decision harder to understandWhat makes Reid's call more interesting is the presence of Justin Tucker. Kansas City recently added the veteran kicker to its practice squad, giving the coaching staff another option if Butker's struggles continue.Tucker brings a strong record from his time with the Baltimore Ravens, having converted 417 of 468 field goal attempts. His experience and previous success naturally raised expectations that he could challenge Butker for the starting job.However, Tucker's arrival does not guarantee an immediate promotion. He has also faced allegations of sexual misconduct from 16 massage therapists, which he has denied. In a statement to OutKick, Tucker said, “I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider,” and added, “I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists.”Reid's decision has drawn criticism from Chiefs supporters, several of whom questioned why the team would keep Butker in place after bringing in Tucker. One fan wrote, “Insanity is doing the same exact thing and expecting a different outcome,” while another suggested Kansas City should be prepared to go for it on fourth down in Atlanta territory.The Falcons game now offers Butker another chance to ease the pressure. If his struggles continue, Kansas City may have a much harder decision to avoid in Week 11.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Kyle Van Noy and wife Marissa found a deeper meaning in marriage through their beautiful adoption journey
articles.summary: For Minnesota Vikings linebacker Kyle Van Noy and his wife, Marissa, adoption has never been just a family decision.
articles.body: For Minnesota Vikings linebacker Kyle Van Noy and his wife, Marissa, adoption has never been just a family decision. It is part of their shared history, one that shaped their relationship long before they became parents. Both grew up with close ties to adoption, giving them an understanding of what it means to welcome a child into a family. That connection later influenced their charitable work, their own journey into parenthood and Kyle's decision to learn more about his biological background.Adoption became the foundation of Kyle and Marissa's relationshipAdoption was one of the first things Kyle and Marissa discovered they had in common when they met in college. Kyle was adopted by Layne and Kelly when he was barely two months old, while Marissa's father and younger brother were also adopted.“It’s the foundation of us,” Marissa, 34, tells PEOPLE in celebration of Adoption Month.The subject came up early in their relationship, possibly during their first date. Marissa remembers the adoption of her younger brother particularly well. She was 11 at the time and watched her family go through the process of bringing him home.“Just wanting for years to have that missing puzzle piece in our family and then finally having it. I start crying every time I talk about it, but I love my little brother so much. He’s definitely the missing puzzle piece to our family,” Marissa shares through tears.Kyle's experience was different, although his family made sure he never felt out of place. Around the age of five or six, he began noticing that he did not physically resemble the other members of his extended family. With both his parents having six siblings, family gatherings often made that difference more noticeable.“And my parents both have six siblings on each side, so when we were around family, I’d be like, ‘I don’t look like anybody,’ ” Kyle recalls.His mother, however, remained protective of him and his brother Travis. Kyle says his parents did not discuss adoption in detail until he reached high school. His mother eventually became comfortable with him exploring his biological family history.“So it took her a while, but I’m grateful, she has always been supportive, she has always been my mom, so that’s my mother,” says Kyle.One memory from his teenage years still makes him smile. During a Walmart trip with Travis, a woman noticed the two boys and confidently told them she could see their resemblance. For Kyle, it was a reminder that family goes beyond physical similarities.Fatherhood gave Kyle another reason to explore his rootsKyle and Marissa turned their personal connection with adoption into action after his NFL career began. In 2014, shortly after he was drafted, they established the Van Noy Valor Foundation to support adopted, foster and disadvantaged children.Their own family grew when Marissa became pregnant with their first child, Trae, in 2019. That experience prompted Kyle to look more closely into his biological background, particularly after doctors asked him questions about his medical history.Marissa remembers how difficult it was for him to provide answers.“I think that sparked a lot of interest for him, just knowing medically and genetically.”Kyle eventually gathered the information he needed. When their daughter Giavanna was born in 2022, he felt far more prepared to answer the doctors' questions.“I was more comfortable when the doctors were asking questions when my daughter was born. I didn’t feel dumb this time around. I felt like I knew, and that was the main reason why we did it and got all the information we needed,” says Kyle.The foundation has also given the couple an opportunity to connect with families facing experiences similar to their own. Marissa says meeting children, listening to their stories and offering encouragement have been among the most rewarding parts of their work.For her, seeing young people recognise what Kyle has achieved carries a special meaning. His journey offers them a reason to believe that their own circumstances will not define their future.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 10 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers who invested a lot in the Los Angeles Rams offense are having a hard time finding healthy players in the team's passing attack. Also, it'll be tough to find a replacement for Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who's on a Week 10 bye.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers who invested a lot in the Los Angeles Rams offense are having a hard time finding healthy players in the team's passing attack. Also, it'll be tough to find a replacement for Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who's on a Week 10 bye.

The Rams are without their top two wide receivers, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and high-upside, second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson, who flashed in Week 2.

Quarterback Matthew Stafford could turn two under-the-radar Rams pass-catchers into fantasy studs this week.

If you prefer to look for unheralded fantasy gems elsewhere, check out Thursday night's game between the New York Giants and the Washington Commanders, where you can find a fill-in for Williams. You can also target the New England Patriots' matchup against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

By the way, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs could miss two to three weeks with a broken ring finger. Circle back to the Packers' backup running backs who saw touches early this season.

Here are the top eight sleepers for Week 10—all available in at least 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros ' consensus roster percentages.

QB J.J. McCarthy vs. Washington Commanders (22 Percent Rostered)

J.J. McCarthy has been efficient since taking over for Jameis Winston, but he hasn't produced high-end fantasy stat lines. The third-year signal-caller has thrown for 622 yards, a touchdown and an interception, with a 63.2 percent completion rate and has rushed for 51 yards on nine carries in three contests.

Thursday night, McCarthy could deliver his best fantasy performance of the season against the Washington Commanders.

The Commanders are allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. They field the 30th-ranked pass defense and have surrendered 16 passing touchdowns in eight games.

With wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely also seeing favorable matchups at their respective positions, McCarthy could put together his first two-touchdown passing performance of the season while in the friendly confines of MetLife Stadium.

QB Geno Smith vs. Buffalo Bills (22 Percent Rostered)

Geno Smith is back on the sleeper radar with a plus matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Don't be fooled by the fact that Buffalo ranks 22nd in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

In the Bills' last two games, they faced the Minnesota Vikings' backup signal-callers, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer, and the Baltimore Ravens' undrafted rookie, Joe Fagnano. Before those matchups, the Bills gave up at least two touchdown passes to five of six opposing quarterbacks.

And sure, Buffalo acquired versatile safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans, but he'll need time to acclimate himself to the team's 29th-ranked pass defense.

If you need a quarterback with Caleb Williams on a bye week, plug Geno Smith into your lineup. He's playing well at home, throwing for seven touchdowns and two interceptions at MetLife Stadium.

Furthermore, wide receiver Garrett Wilson could pass concussion protocol in time for Sunday's contest after missing last week's game, giving the Jets' aerial attack a much-needed boost in what could be a high-scoring contest. FanDuel set the total points line at 50.5 for this game.

RB Corey Kiner vs. Detroit Lions (10 Percent Rostered)

Headed to Munich, Germany, the New England Patriots will have a new lead running back in Corey Kiner.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Rhamondre Stevenson could miss "a short period of time" because of a knee tendon issue. TreVeyon Henderson will miss his third consecutive game because of illness.

Kiner has been productive in a complementary role, averaging an impressive 4.9 yards per carry, and he scored his first NFL touchdown last week, logging eight carries for 55 yards in a blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers.

Although the Patriots haven't featured Kiner in the short passing game (two catches for 16 yards), he should get most of the touches against the Detroit Lions. With the 24-year-old averaging nearly five yards per carry, he has a chance to make big plays and reach paydirt in consecutive weeks despite a tough matchup.

RB Pierre Strong Jr. vs. Minnesota Vikings (2 Percent Rostered)

The Green Bay Packers will likely revert to a backfield committee in the absence of Josh Jacobs, who needs time to recover from surgery on his broken finger .

Before Jacobs' return from the commissioner's exempt list in Week 7, Pierre Strong Jr. led the Packers' backfield with 16 touches, logging 11 carries for 28 yards and five receptions for 39 yards while MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson were active.

Lloyd isn't on the injury report after sitting out last week with a knee injury. He'll likely split early-down carries with Johnson.

Nonetheless, Green Bay hasn't been efficient at running the ball, and even less so without Jacobs. You're banking on Strong's involvement in the short passing game for a solid fantasy return. It's a reasonable risk to take, with the Packers likely to expand his role this week.

WR Treylon Burks at New York Giants (5 Percent Rostered)

Treylon Burks has made his contributions as the Washington Commanders' big-play receiver this season. He carved out a more consistent role after lead wideout Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in a Week 6 outing against the San Francisco 49ers.

Burks has drawn at least five targets in each of his three appearances since Week 5. He missed the team's most recent game because of a foot injury.

He isn't on the Commanders' final injury report for Thursday's game, so he should be good to go against the New York Giants, who are stingy with giving up receiving yards but have allowed 14 passing touchdowns in eight contests.

Averaging 19.4 yards per catch, Burks only needs a few receptions to be a decent flex option. Over his last two games, he's caught seven passes for 147 yards. Don't sleep on him Thursday night.

WR Konata Mumpfield at Arizona Cardinals (5 Percent Rostered)

Konata Mumpfield has the best chance to emerge as the Los Angeles Rams' No. 1 wide receiver with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on the sideline. He showed flashes of what he can do, stretching the field in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos, hauling in four of eight targets for 93 yards and a touchdown.

In that game, Mumpfield served as the No. 2 receiver behind Adams while Nacua sat out with hip and groin injuries.

Now, as the Rams' potential lead wideout, Mumpfield could have a full breakout game against the Arizona Cardinals, who are tied for 13th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers and have allowed 19 passing touchdowns in nine contests.

Expect the Rams to run the ball with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but when quarterback Matthew Stafford drops back, Mumpfield should be one of his primary reads against a vulnerable pass defense.

WR Jordan Watkins at Dallas Cowboys (3 Percent Rostered)

The San Francisco 49ers have a wide receiver corps of mostly older veterans, though 24-year-old Jordan Watkins is emerging. Over the last two weeks, he's caught seven passes for 142 yards and a touchdown.

On Wednesday, wideout Deebo Samuel Sr. was limited in practice and could return Sunday from a hamstring injury, but Mike Evans remains out with an Achilles injury.

With Evans sidelined, Watkins will likely remain involved in the 49ers' passing attack, particularly if Samuel also misses another game—even with the addition of Keenan Allen, who primarily lines up in the slot.

Watkins has a chance to feast on the Dallas Cowboys' pass defense, which is giving up the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Possibly as the No. 2 receiver in a plus matchup, he doesn't need to score a touchdown to produce a solid fantasy stat line.

Nonetheless, FanDuel set the point total at a whopping 55.5 for this game, so we could see several touchdown drives for both teams.

TE Colby Parkinson at Arizona Cardinals (4 Percent Rostered)

Without Terrance Ferguson, the Los Angeles Rams can still feature a deep tight end group in the passing game, though Colby Parkinson is the one you want in your lineup.

Over the previous three weeks, Parkinson has hauled in 14 of 16 targets for 92 yards and a touchdown. In the same stretch, 11th-year tight end Tyler Higbee has been inefficient in the passing game, hauling in four of his 10 targets for 41 yards.

Aside from a two-touchdown game against the Las Vegas Raiders, fourth-year tight end Davis Allen hasn't seen many looks in the passing game. Rookie second-round tight end Max Klare has yet to record a reception.

Parkinson is on the injury report with an oblique injury, but he participated in a limited practice session to start the week.

Keep an eye on Parkinson's status, though barring a setback, he could finish No. 1 or No. 2 in targets for the Rams' depleted pass-catching group, which is notable against the Arizona Cardinals, who allow the eighth-most fantasy points to tight ends.

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 10 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: In Week 10, NFL bettors will have to weigh unknown factors in a few games. Three quarterbacks are slated to make their first career starts on Sunday. How will Fernando Mendoza, Carson Beck and Kyle McCord impact the complexion of their games?
articles.body:
In Week 10, NFL bettors will have to weigh unknown factors in a few games. Three quarterbacks are slated to make their first career starts on Sunday. How will Fernando Mendoza, Carson Beck and Kyle McCord impact the complexion of their games?

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , weighed the variables and mostly sided with experience. Yet a few of our experts made a case for the new faces at quarterback to help their teams at least cover the spread this weekend.

Before we get into the breakdowns for the 14-game slate, check out the standings against the spread below.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Washington Commanders (2-5-1) at New York Giants (5-2-1)

These teams tied the last time they faced one another, though the rematch will look a little different. New York will have home-field advantage in this one, and it will have J.J. McCarthy in at quarterback instead of Jameis Winston.

McCarthy has mostly played well since joining the Giants, and he and Cam Skattebo both appear to be healthy enough to go this week. On the other side of the ball, rookie Arvell Reese has become a legitimate game-wrecker. I totally understand why most of the panel is backing New York here.

However, I also get the feeling that we could see McCarthy stumble on a short week and against a defense that can largely corral the run. If the Commanders can contain Reese, they can steal one on the road.

This game will ultimately define the Giants. The last time a matchup like this came up on the schedule—home vs. the Saints in Week 6—they lost. This is a game they need to win to justify their NFC East lead and prove they're better than just wading through the NFL's weakest schedule to date.

Should they lose, they'll probably wind up losing the division. Former Giants coach Bill Parcells used to say, "You are what your record says you are," and at this point in the season, the Giants either prove they're for real (at least in a division-leading sense) or we buckle up for a brutal second half of the season.

Giants: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Moton, Sobleski

New England Patriots (5-4) vs. Detroit Lions (6-2)

I'd buy up to a full field goal if you can, but this will be a very tight game at a neutral site.

Detroit's defense has certainly improved, but a still-vulnerable unit is due for a blip. New England leads the AFC with 41 20-plus-yard plays ( 33 passing and eight rushing ), while the Lions have given up an NFL-high 40 ( 34 passing and six rushing ).

This feels like a correction game for a Pats team that hasn't lost back-to-back games since December 2024.

After watching Jordan Love throw for 372 yards and three touchdowns on the road against the New England Patriots, you have to wonder what the Detroit Lions' eighth-ranked passing attack can do offensively in Munich, Germany.

Coming off two modest outings against the Vikings' second-ranked pass defense and the Miami Dolphins in humidity, Jared Goff is due for a strong performance in a favorable matchup.

The Patriots have allowed multiple touchdown passes in three straight games, and they lack the offensive firepower to keep pace with high-scoring opponents, even if star wideout A.J. Brown plays at less than 100 percent with a knee injury. Goff will heavily target Amon-Ra St. Brown, who has dual citizenship in both the United States and Germany, allowing him to shine in a game that means a lot to him .

Lions: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Minnesota Vikings (6-2) at Green Bay Packers (6-3)

This spread appears to indicate that Vegas views these teams as relative equals. They aren't—at least not right now.

Minnesota's ultra-aggressive defense could be a problem, especially for a Packers team that can't run the ball. But the Vikings offense remains a liability until we see differently, and Green Bay's defense is better than most realize.

Throw in Jordan Love shredding secondaries of late, and Green Bay covers at Lambeau.

The Packers' passing attack is white-hot, and Jordan Love probably isn't getting enough attention as an MVP candidate.

However, I think Minnesota is primed to cool things off in a hurry. The Vikings have the best defense in the league right now, and I don't think it's particularly close.

Had Minnesota had any semblance of a competent offense on Monday night, it probably would have knocked off Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills.

The addition of Kirk Cousins should instantly give the Vikings the most functional offense they've had all season. He won't have a lot of time to prepare for this matchup, but he knows the offense and knows how to get Justin Jefferson involved.

I expect Cousins to start, and I expect to hear a lot of talk about how the Vikings "stole" him at the trade deadline.

Packers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Houston Texans (3-5) at Cleveland Browns (5-4)

I'm the only one riding the Browns to cover here. It's easy to see Deshaun Watson getting sacked 10 times against a Texans defense leading the league in sacks, but the Browns are 3-0 at home this season for a reason. Cleveland is a difficult place to play.

The Texans probably see this as a revenge game as much as Watson does, but I think the Browns are able to muddy this one up for C.J. Stroud just enough to stay in the game, like we've seen them do multiple times this season.

The Browns defense should be able to slow Stroud and the Houston Texans offense, but it won't be enough when Cleveland fields an anemic offense that ranks among the bottom four in scoring.

It doesn't matter which quarterback is starting for the Browns, because the Texans defense should make their life miserable, even if that unit has been somewhat of a disappointment this season.

Texans: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) at Atlanta Falcons (3-6)

There are some tempting hooks on home underdogs this week, and this is a good example. All things considered, the Chiefs are not playing great football. They're also just 2-2 with a negative scoring margin away from Arrowhead.

The Kansas City pass rush woke up last week, but that unit has struggled overall and runs into one of the league's top pass-protection units here.

I think this game will be decided by a field goal.

The Chiefs and Falcons made two of the most interesting deals prior to Tuesday's trade deadline for entirely opposite reasons. Atlanta traded safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars even though he was the team's best defensive player.

Conversely, the Chiefs added Josh Downs, who is one of the league's best slot receivers. Bates' absence in the Falcons' secondary coupled with Downs' potential impact for a Kansas City offense that has failed to create explosive plays shows the difference in the teams' philosophies and which squad should be considered a more serious threat.

Chiefs: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Miami Dolphins (1-7) at Indianapolis Colts (2-7)

Neither offense inspires much confidence heading into this matchup. Miami will give Kyle McCord his first career start, while Indianapolis has limited options at wide receiver. Even with that uncertainty at quarterback for the Dolphins, I expect a close game. I'll take Miami and the points.

This matchup would have been the perfect time for some of the Dolphins' young players to experience a breakout game. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Malik Willis is now on injured reserve, and second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord will make his first career start.

The Colts didn't trade everyone, and plenty of talent can still be found in the Indianapolis secondary to confuse a first-time starter. Plus, Jonathan Taylor remains a Colt, so the Indianapolis offense can still feature a strong run game.

Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-7)

It's not easy to back a team that just held a fire sale against a team that just completed a shopping spree, but a line in this range reflects that. Tennessee has had two weeks to prepare, and the Titans have lost by more than seven points just once since Week 2. The Jags still win this game, but I do expect some growing pains as the new personnel settles in.

I am worried about a backdoor cover, but the Jaguars enter this divisional matchup on the heels of officially going "all-in" courtesy of big, splashy trade deadline moves. This team wants to make a statement on both sides of the ball. Expect Liam Coen's offense to roar from the opening kickoff and let the defense feast on a bad Titans offense as they genuinely put the league on notice.

Jaguars: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Carolina Panthers (3-5) at New Orleans Saints (3-5)

Granted, New Orleans' latest victory came against a very inconsistent Browns team and easily could have been a loss—the outcome ultimately hinged on an overtime two-point play. However, I thought the Saints looked like a much more complete team coming out of the bye than they were heading into it.

New Orleans' pass rush was legitimately good against Cleveland, and it should be a problem for a Panthers O-line that's been about as sturdy as a jack-o'-lantern in mid-November. Audric Estimé provided some punch to the ground game, and Jordyn Tyson gave Tyler Shough another weapon.

I do have concerns about the Saints' ability to contain Chuba Hubbard and Carolina's rushing attack, but I still think we'll see the Panthers' losing streak extended to four games.

Although the Carolina Panthers are on the road, it's a good bounce-back spot for a team on a three-game losing streak. The Panthers can get back to pounding the ball on the ground against the New Orleans Saints' 29th-ranked run defense. In doing so, they can avoid turnovers after giving the ball away eight times over the last three weeks and control this game.

Panthers: Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Buffalo Bills (7-1) at New York Jets (2-7)

After a big win in Minnesota, there's reason to worry about a letdown in another road game for a Bills team that has been inconsistent defensively this season. But Buffalo has an offense that can put up 30 against anyone, while the Jets look scrappy offensively one week and inept the next.

It's the same old Jets, but these Bills just might be different.

This is yet another tricky hook with an away team, and in this case the banged-up Bills are on short rest against an opponent that is quite familiar with them. The Jets may be 2-7, but they haven't been outscored by more than a handful of points in any of their four home games. I think they'll hang here against a tired opponent.

Bills: Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Davenport

Los Angeles Rams (5-4) at Arizona Cardinals (3-6)

It's unlikely the Rams forget that the Cardinals upset them earlier this season. That doesn't bode well for a team that is winless at home and will start rookie QB Carson Beck, who is making his NFL debut.

The Rams have issues of their own with Puka Nacua set to miss extended time , but the Rams' defense will make life difficult for Beck in his first start, while Sean McVay leans on his run game against a defense that has struggled to stop the run all season.

Both teams will be missing key players, but the Rams still have quarterback Matthew Stafford and, arguably, the NFL's best running back duo in Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Stafford won't throw for a ton of yards, but Williams and Corum could rush for 200-plus combined against a defense that's allowed 120-plus yards in five out of nine contests.

Meanwhile, rookie third-rounder Carson Beck will make his first career start. He's a third-string quarterback with little around him aside from All-Pro tight end Trey McBride.

Rams bracket McBride in coverage and physically wear down Arizona's defensive front to avenge their shocking Week 6 home loss to the Cardinals.

Rams: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Seattle Seahawks (5-4) at Las Vegas Raiders (4-5)

I'm the only one backing the Raiders in Fernando Mendoza's first career start, and I'm OK with that. The Raiders defense has been leaking points, but with Drew Lock in line to start again for the Seahawks, I'm not banking on Seattle hanging 30 this week.

The Vegas home crowd will be energized to see their No. 1 pick take the field, and I believe in Mendoza's ability to answer the call. Look for the rookie to keep this game close. Seattle wins a must-win game for its playoff hopes, but the Indiana product reminds everyone he was worth the wait.

Las Vegas pulled off a blockbuster trade deadline move, sending Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, which means No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is slated to make his first career start. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak will compete against the team he helped lead to a Super Bowl victory last season.

Despite the familiarity with some of the Seahawks players, Kubiak is working with an inexperienced starting quarterback against an elite-level defense, and his team has tied an NFL record for allowing 30-plus points in six straight games.

Raiders take a step back in a loss by more than a touchdown before they start to see Mendoza make strides.

Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

San Francisco 49ers (7-1) at Dallas Cowboys (4-5)

While no one outside of the Cowboys should have any confidence whatsoever that the Dallas defense can slow the 49ers offense, an opposite viewpoint can be taken when Dak Prescott and his offense are on the field.

The Cowboys have scored 27 or more points in three straight games. They'll be able to move the ball, even against the Niners' talented defense, which could turn this game into a shootout and potentially keep it close.

This classic rivalry is always good for a surprise. The Cowboys keep disappointing while the 49ers keep persisting despite never seeming fully healthy, and I heavily debated taking the points because this feels like a trap.

I'm going to ignore that and believe that the Niners are the NFL's best team and that Dallas cannot get out of its own way.

49ers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) at Cincinnati Bengals (6-2)

Joe Burrow is the NFL MVP as of today, but the Bengals won't coast to a win here (if they win at all). The Steelers come into this one off their bye and rested, while the Bengals played in Spain last week. Being at home will help, but I don't expect that to do a Bengals defense that's struggled mightily this season any favors.

I expect a heavy dose of Jaylen Warren in this one, and I think the Bengals struggle to get consistent stops. This feels like a game that turns into a shootout, but three of these teams' last four meetings have been decided by a field goal or less and this one won't be any different.

Cincinnati's offense seemingly flipped a switch during the bye week, and I'm not sure there's a better unit in the league right now. The Bengals lack the balance that comes with a quality ground game, but Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins have looked borderline unstoppable.

The Steelers can limit the Bengals by attacking an offensive line that still isn't good enough. However, I don't think they can shut down Cincinnati for a full four quarters.

Pittsburgh's best bet will be to lean on the run and keep Cincinnati's offense off the field entirely. It's a strategy that could be successful, as the Bengals have struggled badly against the run. I just don't think it'll be enough to counter Cincy's offense and a hyped-up home crowd on Sunday night.

Steelers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) at Baltimore Ravens (4-5)

This is where we are with the Chargers this season—I'm laying a sizable number with a Ravens team starting Jacoby Brissett, who has been with Baltimore all of a week.

The Bolts went 34 drives without scoring a touchdown before finally ending the drought in garbage time of last week's blowout loss. That defeat dropped them to 0-8, and a battered Justin Herbert was sacked eight times.

This is a broken team fixing to get blown out by a desperate one.

I'm not asking for the Chargers to win here. When you watch Justin Herbert and find yourself painfully squinting to discern whether it's really him in that helmet, it's evident that this team is trying so hard to figure things out that they aren't even one of those terrible teams that can luck into a win or surprisingly play better football than expected.

The Chargers are, simply, discombobulated. So, there's no better time to take the points than a road tilt on Monday Night Football against a Baltimore team that is 2-7 ATS this season and 0-4 ATS in home games.

Chargers: Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski
