articles.title: Best Team Fits for Top 10 Bargain Free Agents After 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline has passed, but teams can still fill roster needs with free-agent signings. Typically, clubs make these moves to add depth, though a veteran on fresh legs could provide the boost needed to fuel a deep playoff run.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has passed, but teams can still fill roster needs with free-agent signings. Typically, clubs make these moves to add depth, though a veteran on fresh legs could provide the boost needed to fuel a deep playoff run.

Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk will generate buzz, but he's not a free agent. The San Francisco 49ers reinstated him from the reserve/left squad list, and the league granted them a two-week roster exemption, giving the club until November 23 to make a roster move.

In the meantime, the NFL's top free agents are available to sign with any team, and potential postseason contenders should have a few on their radar.

Here are the top 10 bargain free agents and the best landing spots for them, based on each team's positional needs and the player's schematic fit with that club.

In his prime, Marshon Lattimore matched up one-on-one against Mike Evans in must-see NFC South battles between the New Orleans Saints and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Before the 2024 trade deadline, the Saints traded Lattimore to the Washington Commanders, and he started to show signs of decline.

Last season with the Commanders, Lattimore allowed two touchdowns and a 93 passer rating in coverage; he logged seven pass breakups and an interception. While that's not peak performance, the savvy veteran cover defender was still serviceable in stretches.

Washington released Lattimore before free agency this past offseason. He hasn't signed with a club this year, but the 30-year-old could provide depth for cornerback-needy teams.

Some speculated that the Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions would try to trade for cornerbacks before the deadline. Neither team acquired one. Lattimore could be a solid in-season acquisition for either club.

Best fits: Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions

A few years ago, many regarded Matt Milano as one of the league's most well-rounded three-down inside linebackers. In 2022, he made the AFC All-Pro roster, recording 99 tackles (12 for loss), 10 pressures , 1.5 sacks, 11 pass breakups and three interceptions.

But after that year, Milano struggled to stay on the field. Between 2023 and 2025, he missed 30 games. That said, the versatile linebacker suited up for 12 contests last year, registering 67 tackles (seven for loss), 3.5 sacks and allowing a 77.4 passer rating in coverage.

Milano's contract expired at the end of the 2025 term, and he hasn't resurfaced with another team. Eight months out of action, the 32-year-old may be healthy enough to contribute in a rotational role.

Dallas Cowboys' oft-injured linebacker DeMarvion Overshown sat out Week 9 with a knee injury. Detroit Lions All-Pro middle linebacker Jack Campbell could miss an extended period with a neck injury. Milano could give one of these teams quality snaps at linebacker.

Best fits: Dallas Cowboys, Detroit Lions

Coming out of Temple in 2017, Haason Reddick entered the league as a hybrid defender who can play inside and outside linebacker and settled into a pass-rushing role off the edge in his fourth season.

Reddick logged at least 11 sacks in four consecutive campaigns between 2020 and 2023, but his production declined sharply after the Philadelphia Eagles traded him to the New York Jets in 2024, partly because of a lengthy holdout.

After playing sparingly with Gang Green, Reddick signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2025, logging 31 tackles (six for loss), 2.5 sacks and eight pressures in 13 games (12 starts).

In a designated pass-rushing role, Reddick should be able to make an impact. He could be a solid fit for the Carolina Panthers, who have generated the second-lowest pressure rate at 16.5 percent, or the New England Patriots, who rank 24th in pressure rate at 16.7 percent.

Best fits: Carolina Panthers, New England Patriots

Beset by injuries early in his career, Leonard Floyd didn't miss a game between 2018 and 2024. Though Floyd bounced around the league in his prime, he was highly productive after his four-year stint with the Chicago Bears.

Floyd registered at least 8.5 sacks in five consecutive seasons between 2020 and 2024, helping the Los Angeles Rams win Super Bowl LVI over the Cincinnati Bengals with five tackles and a sack.

In 2025, with the Atlanta Falcons, Floyd played in a reduced role and saw the field for a career-low 49 percent of the defensive snaps . He finished the campaign with 19 tackles (five for loss), 3.5 sacks and 19 pressures .

At 34, Floyd may have lost a step that allows him to close on quarterbacks, but he can still move a signal-caller off his spot with pressure off the edge. The 10-year pro is best suited as a stopgap defender.

Floyd can fill a void on the edge for the Cincinnati Bengals, who placed rookie second-round edge-rusher Cashius Howell (wrist surgery) on injured reserve. With the Green Bay Packers, he could spell Lukas Van Ness and Micah Parsons (torn ACL), who, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , is targeting a Week 12 return.

Best fits: Cincinnati Bengals, Green Bay Packers

Darius Slayton is a big-play receiver who averaged 15 yards per catch in seven seasons with the New York Giants. He racked up 724-plus receiving yards in four of his first five seasons as a primary target in Big Blue's passing attack.

This past offseason, the Giants revamped their wide receiver corps and released Slayton a week before their season opener against the Dallas Cowboys. He briefly reunited with quarterback Daniel Jones when he signed with the Indianapolis Colts, but he didn't play a snap. The Colts released him within a month.

At 29, Slayton can be a productive perimeter playmaker if he can still stretch defenses in the vertical passing game.

According to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette 's Gerry Dulac , the Pittsburgh Steelers discussed trading for wideouts Josh Downs, Brian Thomas Jr. and Calvin Ridley. Yet they didn't acquire anyone before the trade deadline.

The Los Angeles Rams will be without their top two receivers, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, for the foreseeable future. Matthew Stafford needs an experienced starting wideout to target within the Rams' depleted pass-catching unit.

Best fits: Los Angeles Rams, Pittsburgh Steelers

After eclipsing 1,000 rushing yards in four consecutive seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Najee Harris has struggled to find career stability on a second team.

On a one-year, $5.25 million contract, Harris appeared in only three games with the Los Angeles Chargers before tearing his Achilles tendon in September 2025.

This year, coming off an injury, Harris signed another single-term, prove-it deal with the New York Giants. They released him six weeks into the season after he publicly expressed dissatisfaction with his role. The 28-year-old running back has been a free agent since then.

Nonetheless, Harris could be an asset to a team that needs a short-yardage tailback. He's a 6'1", 242-pound bruising ball-carrier who can pick up first downs in critical situations and close drives near the goal line.

New England Patriots' lead tailback Rhamondre Stevenson may miss time with a knee injury , and TreVeyon Henderson is set to miss his third straight game with a neurological issue . Entering Week 10, Corey Kiner is the Patriots' lead running back. Harris could be the No. 2 option out of the backfield.

Dallas Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones expects backup running back Tyler Goodson to miss time with a knee injury. The Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to their practice squad, but he has a history of injuries. Harris could be a solid complement to Javonte Williams in the Cowboys' ground game.

Best fits: Dallas Cowboys, New England Patriots

Taylor Decker may be waiting for the right situation to sign with a contender. He's a 33-year-old career left tackle who earned a Pro Bowl nod in 2024. After 10 seasons, his tenure with the Detroit Lions ended after he refused to take a pay cut . The 10-year veteran requested his release.

Despite his departure from Detroit, Decker still believes he can perform at a high level, though he will likely need to lower his salary demand in negotiations at his age.

Nonetheless, Decker plays at a position where quality players are in high demand. He could return soon if a playoff contender needs stronger protection for its quarterback.

The Carolina Panthers are trying to get back to the postseason, but Bryce Young has taken a lot of hits. He's already taken 26 sacks, just one fewer than all of last season. Left tackle Rasheed Walker is struggling in pass protection, allowing five sacks on 367 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus .

The Pittsburgh Steelers should consider reshuffling their offensive line, moving Troy Fautanu back to right tackle over rookie first-rounder Max Iheanachor and signing Decker to play left tackle.

According to Pro Football Focus , Iheanachor has allowed five sacks on 251 pass-blocking snaps.

Best fits: Carolina Panthers, Pittsburgh Steelers

C.J. Gardner-Johnson's career path would make for an odd case study. He brings tremendous value to a secondary with his versatility. The eight-year pro has played a significant number of snaps in center field as a deep safety, in the box and in the slot, logging 396 tackles (27 for loss), 57 pass breakups, 21 interceptions and seven sacks.

Yet Gardner-Johnson hasn't played more than three seasons with a team. He's bounced around the league with six clubs, suiting up with a different squad every year since 2022.

Gardner-Johnson's constant movement raises questions about his fit in locker rooms and his temperament. This year, he played 90 percent of the defensive snaps across six appearances with the Buffalo Bills before the team released him.

Teams interested in Gardner-Johnson should view him as a short-term rental, though he's a chess-piece defender who can do a little bit of everything on the back end. The Atlanta Falcons could consider him after trading Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Dallas Cowboys need help for their 25th-ranked scoring defense.

Best fits: Atlanta Falcons, Dallas Cowboys

NFL teams considering Tyreek Hill would need to evaluate his recovery from serious knee injuries.

They would also have to consider the outcome of a civil trial involving his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro. According to the Associated Press , a Miami jury found Hill liable for two battery claims and not liable for eight other claims.

Hill's injury recovery and the civil jury's findings could factor into teams' evaluations, though a team willing to sign him may still see potential for the explosiveness that made him a game-changing receiver.

Between 2022 and 2023, the 32-year-old averaged more than 100 receiving yards per game and led the league with 13 touchdown receptions in 2023. He played with torn wrist ligaments and still registered 81 catches for 959 yards and six touchdowns in 2024.

In the following campaign, the dynamic wideout played only four games before suffering season-ending knee injuries that have sidelined him to date.

In October, Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he's in talks with "multiple teams" regarding his client's status, with the goal of the receiver joining a club in the "immediate future."

We may hear buzz about Hill's return after Thanksgiving, the late stretch of the season when teams push for playoff berths and seeding.

Even with the addition of wideout Josh Downs, the Chiefs may consider reuniting with Hill to add another playmaker for Patrick Mahomes. The Los Angeles Rams may also keep tabs on him, since Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are both sidelined with injuries.

Best fits: Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams

Even at 36, Bobby Wagner is a premier talent who also brings invaluable intangibles to a locker room. The 10-time Pro Bowler and six-time All-Pro is a proven field general who's recorded at least 104 tackles in every season of his 14-year career. He's also been an iron man in recent years, suiting up for all 17 games between 2022 and 2025.

Last season, Wagner manned the middle of the Washington Commanders defense, recording 162 tackles (eight for loss), 4.5 sacks, 11 pressures , four pass breakups and two interceptions while allowing an 89 passer rating in coverage.

Although Wager isn't an elite cover defender, he can still play on all three downs as a defensive centerpiece. Any team that needs someone to solidify its front seven should consider reaching out to his agent.

If the Detroit Lions expect linebacker Jack Campbell to be out for the long term with a neck injury, Wagner would be a logical addition to their defense. He could also be a fit alongside the Cincinnati Bengals' young linebackers, Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight, to bolster their run defense, which is allowing five yards per carry, the most in the league.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Updated Fantasy Football Week 10 Trade Value for Top 50 NFL Players
articles.summary: Wanna make a deal?
articles.body:
Time is running short to improve your team via trade, with the fantasy trade deadline approaching. And after all of this week's real-life trades and injuries, the landscape of your team might look quite different. If you find yourself in the market for some upgrades, the fantasy football trade value chart is here to help.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

This week, in particular, has seen fantasy trade values massively impacted by injuries and splashy trades.

Puka Nacua, Josh Jacobs and Rhamondre Stevenson aren't trade considerations given their recent injuries and uncertain recovery timelines.

The Arizona Cardinals have enormous uncertainty at quarterback, while the loss of Michael Wilson for the season means defenses are going to be able to fully key on Trey McBride. It's potentially a double whammy for his fantasy value, though the counter-argument is that there isn't much competition for targets.

Kirk Cousins is a huge boon for the fantasy value of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Tuesday was a very good day for fantasy players who roster Jefferson in particular. And while Addison hasn't had a great season, he's a slick player to target in trades, considering you may be able to still buy low.

Fernando Mendoza getting promoted to the starting role in Las Vegas creates some uncertainty in Las Vegas. Brock Bowers should probably be just fine given his massive role in the passing game, but Tre Tucker had a good rapport with Cousins and it's questionable how he'll jell with Mendoza. And it's anybody's guess what Ashton Jeanty's role or production will be going forward.

Whether Josh Downs becomes a flex consideration once again now that he's landed in Kansas City remains to be seen. The passing game likely will continue to still go through Rashee Rice, though going from Daniel Jones to Patrick Mahomes is an enormous glow-up. Regardless, adding weapons for Mahomes increases the quarterback's upside and fantasy trade value.

Keenan Allen's value gets an obvious bump moving to San Francisco, though Deebo Samuel Sr. and Mike Evans (when healthy) are still the upside plays there. But if you can get Allen for cheap, don't hesitate to pull the trigger.

It's been a busy week. Adjust accordingly.

articles.title: Daiyan Henley Trade Called Off by Broncos, LB & Chargers React to Surprise Decision with Funny Posts
articles.summary: Just when you thought the Los Angeles Chargers couldn't suffer further embarrassment during the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Just when you thought the Los Angeles Chargers couldn't suffer further embarrassment during the 2026 NFL season.

The Denver Broncos announced Wednesday night they canceled their trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley.

Henley posted a meme on Thursday morning, and L.A.'s social media team at least had fun with the situation, playfully altering his goodbye graphic when the transaction fell through:

ESPN's Jeff Legwold reported the Broncos didn't disclose why they did a 180. Their trainers may have flagged something from his physical as he went through that process prior to Denver scuttling the trade, per Legwold.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that "it is not uncommon for one team to have some medical concerns about a player while another does not. In this case, Denver had concerns about Henley following his physical."

"Even then, the Broncos still wanted Henlry with Denver and LA discussing revised trade alternatives throughout the day, taking into accounts those concerns," Schefter added. "In the end, no agreement was reached."

Henley has started in all eight of the Chargers' games, and he has missed a total of just three games across his four years in the league. He's first on the team with 51 combined tackles and has one interception and two fumble recoveries.

The 26-year-old would've given the Broncos another option in the linebacking corps for a defense that hasn't been as dominant as it was in 2025.

With the trade deadline passed, Denver doesn't have another avenue to get a player on par with Henley.

The Chargers, meanwhile, lose the 2027 fourth-round and 2028 fifth-round picks they would've received.

Henley is set to be a free agent this offseason. The absence of an extension and his trade to Denver seemingly signal that Los Angeles didn't view him as a long-term piece of the team.

Maybe Henley will do enough in the second half of the season to change the minds of general manager Joe Hortiz and coach Jim Harbaugh.

This wasn't the only deadline-day trade that got voided. The Cincinnati Bengals scrapped a deal for the Philadelphia Eagles' Arnold Ebiketie after initially overlooking the fact they'd lose a third-round compensatory pick as a result of the move.

articles.title: "I just wish I would have...": Donna Kelce's heartbreaking motherhood regret over Jason and Travis Kelce inspires a touching plan for her four granddaughters
articles.summary: Donna Kelce has spent years cheering for Jason and Travis Kelce, but there are parts of their childhood she wishes she could experience again.
articles.body: Donna Kelce has spent years cheering for Jason and Travis Kelce, but there are parts of their childhood she wishes she could experience again. Beyond their football achievements, the brothers had school performances, musical interests and countless little milestones that their mother did not always manage to capture. Now, as she watches her four granddaughters grow up, Donna wants to do things differently. Her latest initiative reflects a personal regret, a grandmother's affection and her determination to stay involved in the girls' lives, even when distance makes it difficult.Donna Kelce opens up about missed childhood moments with Jason and TravisRaising two energetic boys while maintaining a professional career was not an easy task for Donna. The former banker had to balance work commitments with Jason and Travis' growing interests. Looking back, she wishes she had more recordings of their childhood activities, particularly those that happened away from the football field.In a May 2026 interview with Architectural Digest, Donna recalled Travis' interest in playing the trumpet and piano, while Jason learned the saxophone. Their school speeches, debates and performances were also memories she wanted to preserve."And I just wish I would have [also] been able to have that footage."Her admission offers a touching glimpse into the side of motherhood that often goes unnoticed. Parents spend years helping their children discover new interests, but busy schedules can make it difficult to document every special occasion.Donna is also aware that childhood passes quickly. In a November 2023 interview with Us Weekly, she openly expressed her wish to spend more time with Jason's daughters."I wish I could spend more time with them," she admitted.She also explained how she approaches their visits, saying, "When I'm with them, I'm in the moment."Donna Kelce's Gran Cave plan brings her closer to her four granddaughtersDonna now wants to preserve more memories with Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finnley, Jason and Kylie Kelce's four daughters. Her partnership with GameChanger has helped bring that idea to life through the 'Gran Cave', a dedicated viewing space that allows her to follow the girls' sporting and theatrical activities remotely.The setup offers access to live streams, scores and highlights, helping Donna stay connected when she cannot attend an event in person.However, she does not believe technology can replace showing up for family. Speaking to People in May 2026, she shared her philosophy about visiting her grandchildren."Grandparents need to travel to their children. That's just the way it is."She also explained why making an effort matters, saying, "I try to show up."Donna has another piece of advice for Jason and Kylie. She believes children should have the freedom to discover their own interests rather than follow a path chosen for them."Let your children choose what they love to do," she told Us Weekly.She wants her granddaughters to explore sports, music, art and anything else that captures their attention.For Donna, the Gran Cave is about more than watching games. It is a chance to hold on to the childhood moments she wishes she had recorded more often with her sons. This time, she wants to make sure those memories are never too far away.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Broncos, Giants, Browns among teams proving that winning ugly might be good enough this season
articles.summary: It might not be pretty for all the teams currently in the NFL playoff field, but it's working.
articles.body:
Everyone wants to be the mid-1980s 49ers or 1999 Rams, blowing teams out and making their seasons into beautiful highlight reels.

In the NFL in 2026, that might not be possible. Just grinding out wins is good enough.

There are four teams this season who have a winning record despite a point differential of +12 or worse: Broncos, Giants, Patriots, Browns. The Browns are 5-4 despite a point differential of -35. The Broncos have won seven games and six of them came by one score. They barely beat the 0-7 Chargers in Week 5 after trailing with less than 10 minutes remaining.

But they're winning. All of those teams would be in the playoffs if they started today other than the Browns, who are one spot out of an AFC wild-card spot. Other teams like the Steelers and Packers haven't been impressive from Week 1 on, but they're in the playoff field too.

"We found a way to win," has been uttered more than a few times by head coaches of winning teams this season. Winning ugly might end up being the theme of this season.

The Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 sums up how a handful of teams are succeeding this season. The Giants got four field goals and their only touchdown came when Jameis Winston came in off the bench for a drive. From an outside perspective, it was an unwatchable game. But it was pretty good for the Giants.

"We did play winning football, not perfect football, but winning football and found a way to win the game in all three phases, especially starting with the defense," Giants coach John Harbaugh said, via Athlon Sports .

The Giants beat the Titans, who are 1-7, when they intercepted a pass in their own end zone in the final seconds. They beat the Cardinals, who are 3-6, when they intercepted a pass backed up in their own end zone on the final play. The Giants rank 24th in DVOA but are currently the No. 3 seed in the NFC with a 5-2-1 record. For old-school football fans who abhor analytics and care only about a team's record, there's satisfaction in teams winning in intangible ways.

"They have it. They have what it takes," Harbaugh said of his team. "I don't know how to describe it other than that. I think they've had it all along and they found it in these games. Sometimes it's one thing to have it and another thing to find it, and they've been able to find it in the way they play."

The Browns are one spot below the Giants in DVOA, ranking 25th. But they've won more than they've lost. In multiple games this season they've discovered the right answer to the test in the final minutes. In four of five wins they've trailed or been tied in the final two minutes, and in the other win they trailed with four minutes remaining. They're 3-2 in games in which they gain 272 yards or less.

"We don't do anything, and then all of a sudden we get stops," Monken said after a 13-10 win over Baltimore, via the Ravens' site . "All of a sudden we figure it out."

These teams are chasing playoff berths, not trying to hear arguments about regression.

Since the start of the 2025 season, the Broncos are on one of the strangest runs in recent NFL history.

The Broncos are 22-6, counting postseason, and 18 of the wins have come by one score. For those who understand probability, and one-score games in the NFL being practically a coin flip, that record makes no sense.

The Broncos are 7-2 with a point differential of +12. That might be unsustainable, but they did it last season, too. The Broncos have won 16 one-score games in a row, setting an NFL record. That can't continue, but the Broncos truly believe it can.

"Well, when it keeps happening, I think our league is what it is," Broncos coach Sean Payton said after a 26-21 win over the Panthers. "When those things keep falling your way, that's not by accident."

Other teams looked terrible in September and have emerged as contenders for division titles. Packers fans had Matt LaFleur on the hot seat after a bad Thursday night loss to the Falcons dropped them to 1-2. The Steelers were 2-2 after four games and didn't look anything like a playoff contender, but haven't lost since. The Patriots were in trouble at 1-2 and while a blowout loss to the Packers last week was a setback, they're above .500 despite a win differential of just +4.

There might not be a more oft-used quote in the NFL than Bill Parcells' famous line, "You are what your record says you are." And, in truth, the win-loss record is all NFL coaches and players are judged upon. So nobody with a winning record now is making apologies, even if all those victories haven't been pretty.

articles.title: 'Thiccer Kicker' Harrison Mevis' New NFL Landing Spot Revealed in Rumors After Rams Release
articles.summary: One month after being released by the Los Angeles Rams, Harrison Mevis has landed with a new team.
articles.body:
One month after being released by the Los Angeles Rams, Harrison Mevis has landed with a new team.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported Thursday Mevis signed with the Baltimore Ravens to join their practice squad and Riley Patterson was added to their 53-man roster as they look to stabilize their kicking game.

Baltimore's kicker shuffling comes after Tyler Loop was placed on injured reserve last week due to a groin injury. Moody handled kicking duties for the Ravens in their Week 9 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Nicknamed the "Thiccer Kicker" for his 245-pound frame, Mevis originally signed with the Carolina Panthers as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He was waived during the preseason, then caught on with the Birmingham Stallions in the UFL.

After going 20-of-21 on field-goal attempts during the 2025 UFL season, Mevis signed with the New York Jets before being released in September. He signed with the Rams two months later as a replacement for Joshua Karty.

Mevis went 18-of-19 on field-goal attempts and made all 48 extra-point attempts in 12 games between the regular season and playoffs with the Rams last season.

The start of 2026 was rough for Mevis with four misses on nine attempts in five games, including going 3-of-7 from at least 40 yards. He was released by the Rams on Oct. 13, one day after missing two field goals in a 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Thursday will mark the start of Baltimore's practice week as the coaching staff figures out the kicking situation going into a Monday night matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers.

The Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight games to fall into last place in the AFC North. Jacoby Brissett is expected to make his first start for the team after being acquired in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals with Lamar Jackson currently on injured reserve.

articles.title: ‘I’m hoping’ – Patrick Mahomes admits his wife may not love his pregnancy plans
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, shared the news earlier this week that they are expecting their fourth child next year. The Kansas City Chiefs quarte...
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, shared the news earlier this week that they are expecting their fourth child next year.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback is in the middle of the 2026 NFL season and is pushing the Chiefs towards a spot in the postseason. However, the focus remains on making it to the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium in February.

Last year was a stressful one for the Mahomes family after the 31-year-old quarterback suffered a season-ending injury in December. Having battled his way through rehabilitation to return to the field for the start of the season, Mahomes has admitted a stressful run into the early months of 2027 may not be exactly what his wife will be hoping for.

Patrick Mahomes admits Super Bowl run may not be on pregnant wife's preference

Mahomes already has three young children, with the fourth expected next year. A reporter pointed out that when Brittany has been pregnant in the past, the Chiefs have made it to the Super Bowl on all three occasions.

"I'm hoping. I'm hoping. I don't know if Brittany is, but I'm hoping. If we can keep that going and get another Super Bowl win with a baby on the way, that would be awesome, for sure," Mahomes replied during Wednesday's press conference.

"It's a blessing to have another baby on the way. I'm excited for it. I'm hoping that me and Bronze can even up the score, but I'm just praying for a healthy baby at the end of the day."

The Chiefs have got their eyes set on the Super Bowl in February, but they will need to clean up their game slightly following their recent losses to the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos. They were able to add wide receiver Josh Downs to the roster in an attempt to boost Mahomes' offense.

With teams like the Cincinnati Bengals heating up and the Buffalo Bills looking seriously competitive, the Chiefs are going to have to be at their absolute best for Mahomes to get his wish of making it to another Super Bowl.

articles.title: Giants' Malik Nabers Says 'I Kind of Lost Myself' During Recovery from Major Knee Injury
articles.summary: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers discussed in candid detail his lengthy recovery from a torn ACL in 2025.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers discussed in candid detail his lengthy recovery from a torn ACL in 2025.

The third-year wideout told ESPN's Jordan Raanan he "kind of lost myself in the process."

Raanan pointed out that Nabers hadn't suffered a serious injury to that point in his football career. Experiencing this for the first time and not knowing when he'd be back weighed on him.

"Everybody didn't know what my mindset was," Nabers said. "Just at a loss for words. Didn't really have a lot of words to say. Didn't really have, I don't know, I kind of was empty. Just didn't know what the future holds, how I was going to respond, just with everything that was going on. Everybody just didn't know."

The 2024 Pro Bowler added that he struggled to articulate his internal thoughts.

"Just didn't know how to communicate how I was feeling and how things were going because every day it was something new," he said. "... So I just didn't know, I just didn't really see a process. I didn't really see progress from week to week."

The 2026 season got off to an uneven start for Nabers. After an encouraging showing in a Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys, he combined to have six receptions for 27 yards in the Giants' next two games.

Now, the 23-year-old is hitting his stride again. From Week 4 on, he has averaged 110.4 receiving yards per game with two touchdowns.

The Giants have a lot of reasons to be happy as they sit first in the NFC East at 5-2-1. Nabers' reemergence as a No. 1 receiver is among the encouraging signs for the franchise's outlook.

articles.title: Arch Manning Plummets in New NFL Draft 2027 Big Board Rankings Released by Dane Brugler
articles.summary: Arch Manning's draft stock has taken a major hit over No. 6 Texas' 7-2 start to the season.
articles.body:
Arch Manning's draft stock has taken a major hit over No. 6 Texas' 7-2 start to the season.

Manning went from being ranked as the No. 3 overall prospect on the preseason 2027 NFL draft big board from The Athletic's Dane Brugler to slipping out of the top 20 altogether on Brugler's latest edition .

Here's a look at the new top 10 prospects on Brugler's 50-player draft board.

Manning, who was ranked No. 25 by Brugler, has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 2,024 yards with 18 touchdowns and seven interceptions so far this season.

While displaying the athleticism that helped earn him buzz as a potential top draft prospect, Manning has yet to develop consistency during his second full-time season as Texas' starter. He seemingly struggled to read opposing defenses at times during the Longhorns' back-to-back losses to unranked opponents in October.

Manning's struggles have sparked speculation the quarterback could potentially return for another college season rather than entering the 2027 draft.

A few players have remained consistent top-10 prospects since Brugler published his initial rankings in August. That list includes Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith, Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore, South Carolina edge rusher Dylan Stewart, Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons and Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker.

One player who joined Manning in plummeting out of Brugler's top 10 over the first few months of the season is Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, who was considered a candidate to be the top signal caller in the 2027 draft class before suffering a season-ending concussion in September.

Moore has been replaced as Brugler's projected top quarterback by Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker, who ranks second in the FBS with 2,962 passing yards and first with 29 touchdown passes while throwing just eight interceptions during the Cowboys' 6-3 start.

The latest 2027 NFL mock draft by the Bleacher Report NFL scouting department predicts the Los Angeles Chargers will select Smith with the top pick before the Tennessee Titans land on Moore at No. 2.

B/R NFL scouts agree Mestemaker will be the first quarterback off the board. The latest mock draft predicts the Miami Dolphins will select Mestemaker with the third pick of the upcoming draft.

articles.title: Daniel Jones responds to Colts offloading talent at trade deadline: 'You're not happy to see it'
articles.summary: Daniel Jones hated to see the Colts sell off talent at the trade deadline.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday and the Indianapolis Colts exited the day as the team that offloaded the most talent. After trading both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner in the days before the deadline, the team also offloaded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on deadline day.

One player who didn't get moved was quarterback Daniel Jones. After seeing the extent of his team's selloff, Jones admitted he wasn't super happy about the Colts' new direction, per Fox 59.

"Honestly, you're not happy to see it, right?'' he said Wednesday. "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So, you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions. "But . . . it's outside of our control and our job is to play and be prepared to play well. We've got a lot of trust in the guys coming into those spots and we'll be ready to go.''

"Honestly, you're not happy to see it, right?'' he said Wednesday. "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So, you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions.

"But . . . it's outside of our control and our job is to play and be prepared to play well. We've got a lot of trust in the guys coming into those spots and we'll be ready to go.''

It's tough to blame Jones for feeling that way. Following those moves, the Colts' most productive wide receiver is now Laquon Treadwell. He's caught 16 passes for 215 yards in nine games this season.

The options on the depth chart behind Treadwell aren't exactly proven commodities. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is the only other wide receiver on the roster — along with Treadwell — who has at least 100 career receptions. The other three receivers on the Colts' roster — Deion Burks, Ashton Dulin and Anthony Gould — have combined for just 54 career receptions.

It's now up to Jones to make the most of that unproven group.

That could prove challenging. Jones struggled to build on last year's breakout even with Allen and Downs in the lineup. Through nine games, Jones has just six touchdowns against 10 interceptions. He's faced questions about his job security, though he received backing from head coach Shane Steichen.

Despite Jones' struggles, there were some rumors suggesting he could be traded at the deadline. Jones was linked to the Minnesota Vikings, who were desperately in need of a quarterback after backup Carson Wentz struggled in Week 9. Jones had familiarity with the Vikings, as he spent a portion of the 2024 season with the team following his release from the New York Giants. Ultimately, the Vikings decided to bring back veteran Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders.

If it's any consolation for Jones, the Colts did retain his biggest playmaker. Running back Jonathan Taylor was not traded at the deadline, and should continue to be the focal point of the Colts' offense. Jones also still has tight end Tyler Warren, who is now the team's leading pass catcher. Overall, though, it's not the most encouraging group.

The writing has been on the wall for both Jones and the Colts for multiple weeks now. With the quarterback failing to match last year's success, the team's offense cratered. The Colts responded appropriately, selling off short-term parts for long-term help.

That may prove to be the smartest thing for the team in the long run, but it's going to make Jones' job significantly harder in 2026.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Commanders try to put previous nightmare vs. Giants behind them
articles.summary: The Commanders and Giants had a memorable tie in their first meeting.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders should have had a win over the New York Giants this season. Or at least a field-goal attempt for the win.

The last time the Commanders and Giants played, it ended with one of the worst game-management fiascos in recent years. The Commanders were in line for a game-winning 42-yard field goal in overtime. Then it got weird. Washington was painfully slow in running a play from scrimmage in the final minute; Jayden Daniels inexplicably allowed himself to be tackled, and time ran out before Washington could spike it. The game ended in a tie with Washington never getting that field-goal attempt.

Washington is 1-2 since then, and its record this season is a disappointing 2-5-1. The Giants, gifted a half-win in Washington, are 2-1 since then and 5-2-1 overall, good for first place in the NFC East.

The Giants aren't a dominant team, but they're in a great position to win the division and host a playoff game. If the season ended now, they'd be the No. 3 seed in the NFC. Acquiring J.J. McCarthy for a fifth-round pick has had a big impact on their season (and the Vikings' season too). McCarthy isn't coming off his best game — Jameis Winston led the Giants' only touchdown drive in a 19-11 win over the Eagles last week — and is dealing with a hip pointer, but overall he has shown some promise.

The Commanders have been a mess most of the season, and Daniels rightfully said after last week's loss to the Rams that the Giants game is a "must-win." They can't afford a loss. Or even a half-loss like they took when these teams met the first time.

The Commanders' season is practically over, and Dan Quinn's job status might be in jeopardy with a loss on Thursday. If Washington loses, it would be four games behind the Giants and New York would own the tiebreaker. There wouldn't be much reason for hope if that happens. But if the Commanders win, they'd be just two games back and have the tiebreaker. That's a massive swing. The Giants want to get this win to practically eliminate the Commanders and move closer to an NFC East title, but Washington is clearly the more desperate team.

Malik Nabers came into the season with some questions over his health, as he was coming off a torn ACL. But over the first half of the season, he has re-established himself as one of the top young receivers in the NFL. He has 53 catches for 648 yards, and that is after a pretty slow start. He had four 100-yard games in a row, a streak that was snapped last week. In the first meeting with the Commanders, Nabers had 11 catches for 121 yards and a game-tying touchdown with 1:43 left in regulation. The Commanders do not have a cornerback who can reasonably match up with Nabers. Washington is 30th in passing yards allowed and 28th in passing touchdowns allowed. If they can't contain Nabers, it could be a long night.

The New York Giants have a sizable lead in the NFC East and have also been one of the most reliable teams for bettors to back this season (6-2 against the spread). It wasn't pretty, but J.J. McCarthy, Jameis Winston & Co. won (and covered) on Sunday against the Eagles. Although McCarthy left the game briefly with a hip injury, it appears he'll play.

On the other sideline, the Commanders had yet another late-game blunder in a 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 9. Washington is going nowhere fast, and the team has a lot more questions than answers at the moment. It's a little surprising this spread is only New York -2.5, but it's also hard not to back Big Blue at under a field goal. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

The Giants and Commanders played an adorable tie game five weeks ago, with both teams frittering away a likely win in overtime. Thursday night, they get the anticipated rematch. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Will Malik Nabers go off again? Nabers had a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts snapped last week, but this is a great chance to get cooking again. He drew 20 targets and posted an 11-121-1 return the last time he faced Washington's beatable secondary.

2. Can Jayden Daniels get his running mojo back? Daniels needs to run proactively to be at his best, and he gashed the Giants for 103 yards in that prior meeting. He's had just 49 yards rushing, total, in his last three starts. The Washington pass-catchers are ordinary, so if Daniels is going to be a fantasy-worthy start here, he needs to use his athleticism.

3. Is Cam Skattebo back in the Circle of Trust? It's been a whirlwind sophomore year for Skattebo — fumbles, injury, a soft benching. And the Giants did kick the tires on a Jonathan Taylor trade this week. Alas, Skattebo is someone they probably need, given how poorly Devin Singletary played against the Eagles. The Washington run defense has been solid all year, a stark contrast to the pass defense. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Vikings' 'Desperation' for Kirk Cousins Trade, Raiders' Decision to Deal QB
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders decided to trade Kirk Cousins after the Minnesota Vikings increased their offer ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, ESPN's Adam Schefter said Thursday on Get Up.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders decided to trade Kirk Cousins after the Minnesota Vikings increased their offer ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, ESPN's Adam Schefter said Thursday on Get Up .

"What changed is the Vikings' level of desperation, where they went from offering a third-day pick to a third-round pick," Schefter said Thursday.

Schefter added the Raiders' decision also hinged on confidence in 2026 top pick Fernando Mendoza, who wide receiver Tre Tucker said Wednesday has been taking reps with the first-team offense "all year."

"At some point in time, the Raiders know they're going to turn to Fernando Mendoza," Schefter said. "And when you've got a team offering a three, you've got a quarterback who's the No. 1 overall pick in your building, who's taking an increasing number of reps with the starting offense in recent weeks, and the Vikings are after him, and they keep calling— it's time to make the decision to move ahead and to allow Fernando Mendoza to graduate."

The Raiders accepted a 2027 third-round pick Tuesday in exchange for Cousins, setting Mendoza on track to make his first NFL start Sunday against the visiting Seattle Seahawks.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer reported "no one in Vegas was looking to move Cousins" before Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley called Raiders GM John Spytek on Monday.

That discussion took place just before the Vikings started Carson Wentz in place of an injured Kyler Murray against the Buffalo Bills.

"Spytek told Teasley, flatly, that he wasn't looking to trade his starting quarterback, and that, 'You'll have to make us an offer that moves us,'" Breer reported. "Teasley then told Spytek that the Vikings wanted first to see how the Bills game went first, and they'd be in touch."

Wentz and the Vikings lost 23-6 to the Bills Monday night, and Teasley increased his offer from a conditional third-round pick to a guaranteed third-rounder, according to Breer.

Mendoza will now begin his career as an NFL starter with a tough three-week stretch featuring consecutive road matchups against the Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns after Sunday's showdown with Seattle.

The rookie will look to lean on experience from what he described Wednesday as his "mental reps on the sidelines" when taking over for Cousins this weekend against the defending Super Bowl champions.

articles.title: NFL Gameday Guide: Harry Kane's NFL dream, Amon-Ra St Brown in Germany, Kirk Cousins' return and Jordan Love's flying Green Bay Packers
articles.summary: The NFL plays the eighth of its record nine international games in 2026 when the Detroit Lions face the New England Patriots at Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena, live on Sky Sports from 2pm Sunday; Kirk Cousins meanwhile makes his second debut for the Minnesota Vikings after his trade return
articles.body:
Some five years ago, St. Brown spoke to Sky Sports about the importance of his German heritage ahead of entering the NFL Draft. And now he gets to honour it by doing what he does best.

The Detroit Lions will play an international game for the first time since November 2015 this Sunday when they host the New England Patriots at Munich's Allianz Arena.

His mother Miriam hails from Leverkusen and predominantly spoke to the Lions wide receiver and his two brothers in German growing up, while also taking them back to Europe each summer to spend time with their grandparents and play soccer.

St Brown even represented the German national team alongside brother Osiris during his sophomore year of high school, and since landing in the NFL, has worn decals of the German flag on his helmet and returned to host football camps in the country.

St Brown sat his SATs in English, German and French, spent time in French academy Lycee International de Los Angeles, spent a semester in Paris and joined his mother in travelling across the world with trips to Spain, Italy, London, France, the Caribbean, his German home from home and beyond. It was his mother Miriam who revealed the Lions would be playing in Munich on a FaceTime call set up by the Lions back in February.

At long last, he gets to take centre stage overseas as the NFL reaches the final stop on its European tour with the eighth of a record nine international games in 2026.

St Brown brings one of the NFL's most fascinating backgrounds as a ready-made ambassador for the league's increasing global reach, which will be championed by way of its sixth regular-season matchup in Germany since 2022.

His own global connections travel as far as Egyptian nomenclature, after his father John - a three-time Mr World and two-time Mr Universe body-builder - named his son after Amun, the ancient Egyptian deity.

It is Germany the NFL can thank for one of its most gifted players, with St Brown's parents having met at a fitness trade show in Cologne in 1987.

His transatlantic ties have naturally forged a love of soccer as he pitches up in the home of Bayern Munich, where Ballon d'Or-winning England captain Harry Kane has often spoken of his own ambitions to step into the world of St. Brown - as an NFL kicker.

Has he got the leg to do it? Sure. Would it ever happen? Most would say no. Funnily enough, his age by the end of his football career - he is 33 now - is probably a primary reason above all as to why it wouldn't happen.

But will we take advantage of the opportunity to shoehorn Kane's name into a headline? Duh. Clicks pay for this writer's coffee (they don't).

"If I was going to do it, I would take it seriously. I would probably dedicate six months to a year to training," said Kane earlier this year. "Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that it might be a thing where you could connect the two maybe with the seasons."

Regardless, the NFL's global ventures have often amounted to crossover collaboration between its travelling teams and the sporting giants hosting them; last week Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson caught up with Jude Bellingham ahead of their matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals at the Bernabeu, where the likes of Thibaut Courtois, Marc Cucurella and Raphael Varane were in attendance. As far as growing the game is concerned, it is a no-brainer of an easy win.

The Lions arrive 6-2 in a fiercely competitive NFC North, St. Brown continuing to be Jared Goff's prized weapon on the outside with a team-high 61 catches for 657 yards (10th most in the league) and five touchdowns within an offense ranked fifth in yards per game and fifth in scoring.

Detroit have won four straight games, including divisional victories over both the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers in the last three weeks. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs is also at the heart of their success with an NFL-high 1,132 yards and 11 touchdowns from scrimmage.

New England are 5-4 and coming off a 45-27 defeat to the Packers during which Drake Maye, struggling to live up to his MVP-contending heights of last season, threw three interceptions.

The Patriots are battling to swerve a Super Bowl hangover after February's one-sided defeat to the Seattle Seahawks and return to play in Germany for the second time after losing to the Indianapolis Colts in Frankfurt in 2023.

Germany remains one of the NFL's largest fanbases outside of North America, with millions of listeners having previously tuned in to the Armed Forces Network radio station based in Frankfurt during World War II.

The first broadcast out of AFN Frankfurt was on July 15, 1945 from a confiscated house, after which thousands of US troops remained stationed in Germany.

There were later five preseason NFL games in Germany from 1990 to 1994, while the country was also represented by the Hamburg Sea Devils, Rhein Fire, Berlin Thunder, Cologne Centurions and Frankfurt Galaxy in the former World League of American Football/NFL Europe/NFL Europa between 1991 and 2007.

Is there another player in football who reigns as his position's outright No 1 more so than Fred Warner? Arguably not.

The San Francisco 49ers stalwart has occupied top spot among inside linebackers for multiple years now, and remains an unrivalled difference-maker from his role within Raheem Morris' defense.

Warner has been electric in his first campaign back since suffering a season-ending injury in Week Six of 2025, racking up 77 total tackles, five forced fumbles, a fumble recovery, half a sack, 5.5 stuffs and three pass breakups. Few, if any, diagnose the game better than Warner, whose film study is as refined and as expertly-exercised as any player in football.

An incredible sequence against the Las Vegas Raiders last week saw him punch the ball from the hands of Brock Bowers, recover Michael Mayers' fumble in the end zone and deny Kirk Cousins on a quarterback sneak with an incredible leaping stop over center Tyler Linderbaum in the space of about 10 minutes.

Wonder why teams are scared to throw over the middle of the field against the 49ers? Fred Warner.

The Minnesota Vikings would be Super Bowl contenders if they could just figure things out at quarterback, and on Tuesday they rolled the dice once more by trading to bring back Kirk Cousins.

Any scenario in which Justin Jefferson isn't getting the ball thrown his way becomes a major concern; the Vikings had no choice. Kyler Murray could not get it done, the Vikings traded away J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants and on Monday night Carson Wentz epitomised this hobbling offense, which has failed miserably in its bid to back up Brian Flores' defense.

Cousins may be 38 years old, but has been impressive for the Las Vegas Raiders this season and gives Minnesota a significantly better chance of reigniting Jefferson, who has been starved of production.

Cousins is 202 of 315, passing for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and a passer rating of 97.1 as he re-joins the franchise he played for from 2018-2023. Would be quite the story, huh?

Jordan Love is flying, and it feels as though the Green Bay Packers are gathering Super Bowl momentum by the week as their offense begins to takeover.

Love now leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 for 19 touchdowns to six interceptions as the league's most aggressive splash-play merchant.

He ranks first in intended air yards (3,251), intended air yards per attempt (9.5) and completed air yards (1,553) at the heart of the league's second-best passing attack, within which his receivers have notably dropped a league-high 23 passes.

They have become box office viewing, with two No 1 receivers emerging in Christian Watson - third in the league with 879 yards - and Matthew Golden - fourth in the league with 783 yards.

Matt LaFleur has typically built his offense around run game foundations that he can tee off from through the air, but even through the NFL's worst rushing attack he is finding success thanks to Love's arm.

Sunday Night Football stages one of the biggest games of the weekend when the Cincinnati Bengals take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a possible AFC North division decider.

Both sit 6-2 with the Steelers holding the head-to-head advantage after their 30-27 win in the reverse fixture back in September, Jaylen Warren starring out of the backfield on that occasion with 176 yards from scrimmage.

But the Bengals have hit their stride with a four-game winning streak over the last month, Joe Burrow rising to MVP contention while playing some of the best football of his NFL career within the league's most potent passing attack.

Across that four-game span, Burrow has completed 77 per cent of passes for 1,215 yards with 18 total touchdowns, three interceptions and a 132.0 passer rating.

Cincinnati look like legitimate Super Bowl contenders again, producing their best start through eight games since 2015.

The 'super-team' Los Angeles Rams are not looking so super, and there is growing reason to be concerned over their playoff chances this season.

Sean McVay's side were dealt another crushing blow this week when it was revealed Puka Nacua had suffered a right knee injury set to land him on injured reserve and miss at least a month of action, adding to an absentee list already featuring Davante Adams.

Rams General Manager Les Snead is typically one of football's most aggressive dealers, but on Tuesday neglected to add receiver help for Matthew Stafford as they enter Sunday's divisional clash against the Arizona Cardinals 5-4.

McVay is known for his multiple tight end sets, and will now need to lean on as much alongside Kyren Williams and Blake Corum in order to keep this offense afloat

The Jaguars completed trades for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, Falcons safety Jessie Bates III and Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux

Kirk Cousins returned to the Vikings in a trade from the Raiders, who announced No 1 pick Fernando Mendoza as their new starter

The Colts traded wide receiver Josh Downs to the Chiefs and Keenan Allen to the 49ers, while keeping running back Jonathan Taylor

The Rams announced Puka Nacua is likely to be placed on injured reserve with a knee issue

The NFL reinstated wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk to the 49ers after he left the team a year ago

Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew is set to undergo season-ending elbow surgery

Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has the chance to become the second player in NFL history with at least three touchdown passes and a passer rating of 115 or higher in five consecutive games behind Russell Wilson when he faces the Steelers on Sunday night

Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes needs one touchdown pass against the Falcons to overtake Peyton Manning (327) for the most touchdown passes by a quarterback in his first 10 seasons, including the playoffs

With a win at the New York Jets, Josh Allen can surpass Patrick Mahomes (95) for the second-most regular season wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine seasons in NFL history

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs needs a touchdown in Munich to tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns) for the most touchdowns by a player in his first four seasons in NFL history

Packers duo Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have the chance to become the fourth pair of teammates all-time each with at least 900 receiving yards in their team's first 10 games of a season

Myles Garrett needs just half a sack to overtake Jared Allen (128.5 sacks) for the second-most sacks by a player in his first 10 seasons since 1982, when the individual sack became an official statistic

articles.title: Week 10 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fantasy Football Stars to Play and Bench
articles.summary: Week 10 will get underway on Thursday night with an NFC East showdown between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. While neither team in the week's opener made moves at the trade deadline, we saw moves early in the week that will impact the fantasy football landscape.
articles.body:
Week 10 will get underway on Thursday night with an NFC East showdown between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. While neither team in the week's opener made moves at the trade deadline, we saw moves early in the week that will impact the fantasy football landscape.

Kirk Cousins, for example, is the Minnesota Vikings' new starting quarterback. Keenan Allen is now a San Francisco 49ers receiver, while Josh Downs will catch passes for the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Jacksonville Jaguars beefed up their defense by adding Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux.

Injuries will also be a factor this week, and the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be on bye. With all of this in mind, let's examine some starts, sits, and top plays for point-per-reception (PPR) play in Week 10.

Tyler Shough and the rest of the New Orleans Saints offense struggled to get much of anything going early in Week 9. Then, they exploded, as Shough began making plays with both his arm and his legs.

The result for Shough was 19.7 fantasy points and a third straight game with at least 14 points. Shough should have another solid outing against a Carolina Panthers defense that has looked better since the firing of coordinator Ejiro Evero but not necessarily good.

Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. looked like a promising fantasy quarterback early in the season, after he returned from injury and made his 2026 debut. However, he's struggled recently and looked a lot more like the inconsistent quarterback he was in 2025.

Penix had a respectable 14.5 fantasy points in Week 9 but just 2.1 points the previous week. He's likely looking at a down week against a Chiefs defense that has surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing QBs.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Jadarian Price hasn't exactly wowed as a runner since coming off IR, but he's proven to be a reliable receiving option for the Seattle Seahawks. He logged four catches and 11.8 fantasy points in Week 9 and should see a prominent role this week as Drew Lock battles an oblique injury.

Expect the Seahawks to lean on the run and the short-passing game against the Las Vegas Raiders, who have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is set to get his first start against a stiff Seattle defense. Expect Seattle to box in the run and force Mendoza to win through the air, which is problematic for Jeanty.

Jeanty has struggled to make the most of running lanes this season and has seen rookie Mike Washington steal a good chunk of the rushing work. He has some PPR upside but is likely to underwhelm. He had five catches in Week 9 and still finished with just seven fantasy points.

Start: K.C. Concepcion, Cleveland Browns

Denzel Boston has garnered much of the fantasy spotlight for the Cleveland Browns this season, but fellow rookie receiver K.C. Concepcion is starting to shine. He had a 64-yard touchdown pass in Week 9 and finished with 18.8 fantasy points.

The Houston Texans' pass rush will be a problem for Cleveland. The Browns will likely look to counter by using Concepcion's after-the-catch ability on frequent short passes and receiver screens. He should have a high PPR floor against a defense that has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

Rookie Miami Dolphins receiver Caleb Douglas has been a solid flex option, yielding at least eight fantasy points in each of his last three games. He also has a reasonable matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, who have surrendered an average of 24.4 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups.

The problem is that Miami has placed quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve. With Kyle McCord now behind center for the Dolphins, it's impossible to trust Douglas in a fair but not great matchup.

The Dolphins defense has been fairly solid against the pass this season, and the Indianapolis Colts are likely to lean on Jonathan Taylor and the ground game this week. That doesn't bode well for quarterback Daniel Jones. However, Tyler Warren still looks like a strong play in Week 10.

With Allen and Downs both out in Indy, Warren should see a massive chunk of the target share. Miami, meanwhile, has surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

We're likely to see quarterback Jacoby Brissett make his Baltimore Ravens debut on Monday night against the struggling Los Angeles Chargers. He should boost Baltimore's passing attack, but that doesn't mean that managers can trust Mark Andrews.

Andrews has fallen off in a big way this season and hasn't reached double-digit fantasy points since Week 4. The Chargers, meanwhile, have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

articles.title: What to know for the first week after the NFL’s wild trade deadline
articles.summary: We’ve reached the second half of the NFL season after an intense trade deadline, and the playoff races are heating up with one division on pace to make history.
articles.body: We’ve reached the second half of the NFL season after an intense trade deadline and the playoff races are heating up with one division on pace to make history. From Kirk Cousins’ return to Minnesota to a classic rivalry and a Monday night matchup nobody asked for, here are five things to know heading into Week 10. NFC North dominance Never in NFL history have all four teams from the same division made the playoffs, but if the postseason started today, that’s exactly what would happen in the NFC North. The Bears lead the way at 7-2, followed by the Lions and Vikings at 6-2 and the Packers at 6-3. The division’s combined .736 winning percentage is the best through nine weeks since the 1970 merger. It’s also the first division in history to have all four teams at least three games above .500 through Week 9. Perhaps the most impressive stat? The NFC North is a combined 20-3 against the rest of the NFL. Apparently, the only teams that can beat the NFC North are other NFC North teams. Of course, these four teams still have to beat up on each other down the stretch, which should make the race for the division title and potentially the NFC’s No. 1 seed must-see TV. That includes Sunday’s big showdown at Lambeau Field between the Packers and Vikings. Captain Kirk to the Rescue? Can Kirk Cousins ride back into Minnesota and save the Vikings offense? The Vikings sent a third-round pick to the Raiders to reacquire their former quarterback, who spent his best six seasons in Minnesota from 2018 to 2023. And while Cousins is now 38, he’s still putting up big numbers. His 2,340 passing yards and 20 touchdowns this season rank him among the league’s best, with only Joe Burrow throwing more TD passes. On paper, Cousins is exactly what Minnesota needs. The Vikings have been outstanding defensively but rank 31st in passing yards. Monday’s ugly 23-6 loss to Buffalo was their second straight defeat and the third time this season they failed to score a touchdown. The Vikings don’t need Cousins to be Superman. With that defense, even an average offense could make Minnesota a legitimate Super Bowl threat. And if Captain Kirk can turn back the clock? Watch out, NFC. One last early wake-up call Set those alarm clocks one more time! The NFL heads back overseas Sunday as the Lions and Patriots square off in Munich. It’s the eighth of nine international games this season and the final early-morning kickoff, with action getting underway at 9:30 a.m. ET. For Detroit, every win matters in the ridiculously competitive NFC North, making this much more than a sightseeing trip to Germany. The NFL’s international slate wraps up next week when the 49ers and Vikings meet in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football. So enjoy one last Sunday of football with your morning coffee. After this week, you can finally sleep in! Cowboys-49ers: A rivalry renewed One of the NFL’s greatest rivalries adds another chapter Sunday when the Cowboys host the 7-1 49ers in Arlington. San Francisco leads the all-time series 21-19-1 and has won the last four meetings, including two playoff showdowns. Dallas desperately needs a win as it tries to chase down the Giants in the NFC East. Unfortunately for Cowboys fans, this matchup looks like trouble. San Francisco leads the NFL in red-zone efficiency, scoring touchdowns on an incredible 84.6% of its trips inside the 20. Now that offense gets a Dallas defense ranked near the bottom of the league in yards and points allowed. Oddsmakers are expecting a shootout, and fans paying to get into AT&T Stadium better hope they’re right. As of Thursday, the cheapest tickets were going for more than $400, making this one of the priciest games of the season. Worst Monday Night Football game ever? You might want to make other plans Monday night because we’re getting a matchup that could be the weakest “Monday Night Football” game in history. The 4-5 Ravens, losers of four straight, host the winless 0-8 Chargers. Their combined 4-13 record is the worst ever for a Monday night matchup in Week 10 or later. Before the season, Lamar Jackson vs. Justin Herbert looked like appointment viewing. Now? Not so much. Herbert has become the first quarterback ever to go winless while throwing at least one interception in eight straight games to start a season. The Chargers offense also went an astonishing 37 consecutive possessions without a touchdown before finally scoring in garbage time against Houston. THIRTY-SEVEN! Baltimore isn’t doing much better. Jackson is sidelined with a thumb injury, backup Tyler Huntley has a toe injury, and the Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett, who had just been benched by Arizona in favor of Gardner Minshew. Wondering why the NFL doesn’t flex this disaster out of prime time? Unfortunately, Monday night games can’t be flexed until Week 12. So we’re stuck with it. At least one of these teams has to win. Unless, of course, they tie. And that might be the most fitting outcome.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Talks Trade Rumors for 1st Time Since NFL Deadline, Says Colts Have 'Vision'
articles.summary: After the Indianapolis Colts decided against trading him prior to Tuesday's deadline, star running back Jonathan Taylor addressed the rumors that had been surrounding him.
articles.body:
After the Indianapolis Colts decided against trading him prior to Tuesday's deadline, star running back Jonathan Taylor addressed the rumors that had been surrounding him.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Taylor said, "I know that they have a vision and a plan for it. We just gotta execute right now. The best thing that's gonna help us is executing, going out and getting a win vs. Miami."

Taylor added that any discussions regarding a potential trade were "way above [his] pay grade."

The 27-year-old running back was among the biggest names rumored to potentially be on the block leading up to the trade deadline, with ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reporting at one point that "multiple" teams were interested in Taylor and at least one had offered a second-round draft pick and more.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the New York Giants were the team that offered the Colts a second-rounder and more for Taylor.

ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler reported that the Denver Broncos "gave it a run" at Taylor as well, but they weren't "comfortable" with the asking price.

Ultimately, Graziano and Fowler noted that the Colts wanted a first-round pick for Taylor, and no team was willing to go to those lengths.

The Colts traded several other key players ahead of the deadline, sending guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers and wide receiver Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs.

Indy kept Taylor, though, and part of the decision-making process behind that may have been the fact that Taylor is under contract through 2028 and could be a huge part of the Colts turning things around.

This season has been a difficult one, as the Colts are just 2-7, but Taylor has continued to be a standout.

On the heels of back-to-back Pro Bowl selections and 1,400-plus-yard rushing seasons in 2024 and 2025, Taylor is trending toward another big year individually.

Through nine games, he has rushed for 656 yards and eight touchdowns, while also catching 26 passes for 220 yards.

There is little doubt that Taylor will be the focal point of the offense for the rest of 2026 and potentially beyond.

It starts Sunday against the Miami Dolphins in a game the Colts should win, as the Dolphins are just 1-7 and set to turn to Kyle McCord as their starting quarterback with Malik Willis getting placed on injured reserve.

articles.title: Daniel Jones, Jonathan Taylor react to Colts fire sale as they remain put: 'You're not happy to see it'
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor reveals he said farewell to Indianapolis fans before the NFL trade deadline, but the Colts ultimately kept their star running back.
articles.body: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Indianapolis Colts are one of those teams without many key contributors from the beginning of the season after a fire sale amid a struggling campaign. No, running back Jonathan Taylor wasn’t among them, as he stayed put in Indy. But players like wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs joined Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner as trade pieces to other teams. The Colts are clearly rebuilding, and quarterback Daniel Jones and running back Jonathan Taylor – both involved in trade rumors before Tuesday’s deadline -- still have to play eight games this season despite a depleted roster. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Jones admitted not being happy with selling off the pieces owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon and the front office did, but understands this is a business. He knows it, too, after what happened during his time with the New York Giants. "Honestly, you’re not happy to see it, right?" he said on Wednesday while speaking with reporters. "You’re a player and you’re going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So, you’re not happy to see a lot of those decisions. "But it’s outside of our control and our job is to play and be prepared to play well." While talks that Jones could be on the move came later in the trade deadline period, Taylor was the biggest what-if across the league. When the Colts made it clear with the Nelson and Buckner deals that they would be selling assets with just two wins on the year, Taylor’s name was quickly added to the rumors and speculation. The Colts initially said they wouldn’t be accepting phone calls on a possible trade for him, but that tune changed. Teams like the Giants and Denver Broncos came calling, but ultimately, the Colts decided to keep their elite running back in place as well as Jones. "Those are some hard decisions that you have to make," Taylor, who even said farewell to Indianapolis and its fans just in case he was traded after losing to the Dallas Cowboys last week, said in his first comments since the trade deadline passed. "I’m glad I don’t have to make those decisions. I’m glad I just have to come in here, make sure I’m at my best every single day for my coaches and my teammates. So, I would hate to be in that situation. "I know they have a vision and a plan for it, and right now, we gotta execute right now. The best thing that’s going to help us is executing, going out and getting a win against Miami."
