articles.title: Jayden Daniels Dishes on Kobe, LeBron, Tom Brady, Steph Curry's Impact on His 'Chase for Greatness'
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is drawing inspiration from a few all-time great athletes to reach his potential.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is drawing inspiration from a few all-time great athletes to reach his potential.

After Washington defeated the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 8, Daniels went directly to the team's practice facility to work with Commanders strength and conditioning coach Chad Englehart, according to ESPN's John Keim .

That's a habit he picked up from studying his favorite athlete, Kobe Bryant.

Mendoza Praises Cousins as 'Great Mentor'

"It's just the work ethic and the obsession to want to be better and obviously wanting to win," Daniels said. "As I got to learn more about the Mamba Mentality ... Kobe is a huge inspiration for me. You do whatever it takes to win."

The third-year quarterback has also built relationships with all-time great quarterbacks such as Tom Brady and Peyton Manning, and all-time great NBA players like LeBron James and Stephen Curry.

"I have conversations with [LeBron James] all the time," Daniels said. "... Just to hear a perspective of somebody so great that's been at the peak of the sport and media since he came in the league, and how he dealt with pressure and scrutiny."

Daniels was selected with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and he immediately justified his draft position by leading Washington to an NFC Championship Game appearance and earning 2024 NFL AP Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

Since then, Daniels has dealt with his fair share of adversity. The 26-year-old started just seven games in 2025, and his 2026 season has been marred by more injuries and questionable late-game decisions.

"All the great ones have overcome adversity at some point," Daniels said. "Everybody has to deal with it. It's good to just hear a perspective of how other people dealt with it."

The Commanders are heading into a divisional matchup against the New York Giants on Thursday Night Football. Their last game against the Giants ended in a tie after Daniels was unable to clock the ball for a potential game-winning field goal.

articles.title: Marco Rubio spent over $1.2m in taxpayer-funded flights to watch son play college football, despite just four appearances in four years, report claims
articles.summary: Investigative report reveals US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spent over $1.2 million on military flights for personal reasons, raising ethical questions over the use of taxpayer funds.
articles.body: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has come under scrutiny after reportedly using military aircraft for frequent trips to Florida to watch his son play college football, with an investigation estimating that the flights alone cost taxpayers more than $1.2 million. The findings have prompted questions about how often senior government officials should use publicly funded transport for personal commitments, even when their security arrangements require them to fly on military aircraft.Washington Post investigation details Rubio’s trips to FloridaAn investigation by The Washington Post found that Rubio attended at least 10 University of Florida football games over the past two seasons, including five during the current autumn campaign. His son, Anthony Rubio, is a walk-on running back for the university’s team, the Florida Gators.Of the 23 trips Rubio made to Gainesville aboard military aircraft, 15 were classified as personal journeys, according to the newspaper. Using published Department of Defense hourly operating rates for different military aircraft, the Post estimated that the flights had cost more than $1.2 million.Rubio's journeys have frequently involved flying from Joint Base Andrews in Maryland to Homestead Air Reserve Base near Miami, followed by a separate flight to Gainesville. On November 7, he arrived in Gainesville aboard an Air Force C-37, an aircraft commonly used to transport senior government officials, and watched the Gators lose 23-7 to Oklahoma. Anthony did not play in that game.The figures have attracted attention partly because Anthony's playing time has been limited. Now a senior and the third of Rubio's four children, he has appeared in only four competitive games across his four years at the university, including two this season. ESPN statistics show that he has recorded 14 carries for 75 yards and one touchdown during his college career.Why Rubio's travel has raised ethics questionsRubio is required to use military aircraft because of security protocols governing the secretary of state, alongside other senior officials including the secretary of defense and the directors of the FBI and CIA. Those arrangements are intended to ensure that officials retain access to secure communications and can comply with continuity-of-government requirements while travelling.However, the Washington Post reported that Rubio's use of government aircraft appeared to exceed that of his predecessors. Antony Blinken, who served as secretary of state under Joe Biden, reportedly made personal journeys aboard government aircraft “only a couple of times a year”, according to two former officials cited by the newspaper.Government officials travelling on military aircraft for personal reasons must reimburse the public purse the equivalent of an economy-class commercial ticket. That payment, however, is substantially lower than the actual operating cost of the aircraft. Neither Rubio nor the State Department disclosed how much he had reimbursed for the journeys, the Post reported.Cynthia Brown, senior ethics counsel at the nonpartisan watchdog Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, said Rubio's travel appeared “more of an optics issue than a violation”, but argued that the frequency of the trips deserved scrutiny.“If this travel becomes something that is undermining the integrity of your service, are you really taking care of taxpayer dollars the way that you’re obligated to as a public official?” Brown told the Post.“It is something that I think is really important to shine the light on,” she added.Brown noted that while Rubio might not be doing anything that is “technically improper”, he remains the person deciding how often and how far he travels.Rubio defends the trips as State Department pushes backRubio defended his travel in a statement to the Washington Post, saying: “I have and will continue to try and make it to as many events that are important to me personally and to my family as possible.”The controversy has also revived scrutiny of Rubio's previous criticism of government officials' personal use of publicly funded aircraft. In 2023, while serving as a Republican senator for Florida, he called for an investigation into then-transportation secretary Pete Buttigieg's use of government jets for personal travel.Rubio argued at the time: “American taxpayers deserve assurances that their tax dollars are not wasted by the government’s highest officials.” The Department of Transportation's inspector general subsequently cleared Buttigieg of wrongdoing. The review examined eight trips costing a total of $59,000.Dylan Johnson, an assistant secretary of state, rejected comparisons between the two cases in a post on X on Wednesday, describing them as “moronic”.“The Secretary of State (like POTUS, VP, SecWar, and others) is REQUIRED to use military aircraft to maintain access to secure communications at all times and comply with continuity of government protocols,” Johnson wrote.“Pete Buttigieg [was] not a required user of military aircraft.”Johnson said Rubio would continue to use government transport and would reimburse the government “for all personal travel”.“[He] is entirely unapologetic and will continue to attend as many of his family’s events as his jobs allow – that includes his son’s football games for his final year of college football,” Johnson added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Garrett Wilson Rumors Reveal 49ers, Chiefs Interest in Jets Star Before NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs made a run at New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson prior to the NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs made a run at New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson prior to the NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini .

Cimini reported the Jets consider Wilson to be a "foundational piece," so they had no desire to move him.

Injuries prompted San Francisco and Kansas City to look outside the organization to bolster the receiver room. The Niners traded for Keenan Allen, with Josh Downs going to the Chiefs.

Report: Jets Wanted to Keep Roster Intact

The Jets are 2-7 so far. They're building for the future, and general manager Darren Mougey already traded away homegrown stars Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams ahead of the 2025 deadline to accelerate the rebuild. Particularly in the case of Gardner, that looks like a shrewd move .

But New York never gave any indication it was willing to deal Wilson, and the 2022 Offensive Rookie of the Year made it clear he wouldn't press the issue himself.

"Yeah, I want to be here, man," he told reporters in October. "I want to win games and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful."

Wilson would've been better than what the 49ers and Chiefs ultimately got. He has 43 receptions for 527 yards and three touchdowns, putting him on pace to eclipse 1,000 receiving yards for the fourth time in five years.

The four-year, $130 million extension Wilson signed with New York hasn't even gone into effect, either, so he offers a lot of team control.

The thing with a rebuild is that you do need to start building something at some point. Teams in the NFL can also make a quick turnaround with a strong offseason.

The Jets have the draft capital and payroll flexibility to be competitive in 2027. Unless they received a totally overwhelming offer, trading Wilson didn't make a lot of sense.

articles.title: Kewan Lacy injury update makes Ole Miss’ last week even worse after Georgia beatdown
articles.summary: It has been a dreadful week for Ole Miss football. Last Saturday, Ole Miss lost to Georgia 42-7. In the game, Trinidad Chambliss struggled for Ole Miss, thr...
articles.body:
It has been a dreadful week for Ole Miss football . Last Saturday, Ole Miss lost to Georgia 42-7. In the game, Trinidad Chambliss struggled for Ole Miss , throwing for just 170 yards and throwing an interception. Meanwhile, the running game was bad. The Rebels were without Kewan Lacy in the contest. They ran the ball 31 times, including sacks, for just 66 yards.

Now, the running game took another hit on Thursday with an update on the Rebels' star running back , according to Pete Nakos of On3.

"Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to injury, " Nakos wrote.

Lacy has not played since October 24 against Texas, when he dislocated his shoulder. He had previously missed the game against Florida after being injured against LSU the week before. He returned against Vanderbilt. Overall, he ran the ball 78 times for 388 yards and five touchdowns. Further, he caught ten receptions for 33 yards. Lacy had already been ruled out for this week against Oklahoma , and now his absence will extend to the rest of the season.

This is not a complete surprise based on the update head coach Pete Golding gave following the game against Texas.

"Obviously he's not going to play this week, and then we're going to evaluate that moving forward what that looks like," Golding said. "So, I know [I] normally wouldn't tell you that, but there's no chance that we're going to try that at all this week. He's still [going] through the rehab process. We're still getting some MRIs and all that stuff, but it was definitely a different injury than what it was."

Lacy was coming off a dominant 2025 season in which he ran for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns. This led to All-American honors for the running back. He is eligible for the 2027 NFL Draft and could still be one of the top running backs picked if he chooses to go pro. He could also decide to return to school for another season.

With Lacy out of the lineup, Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight will be the primary backs. Frazier has run for 375 yards but has not scored. Meanwhile, Mills-Knight has run for 165 yards and three scores this year.

articles.title: Giants are winning games under John Harbaugh they used to lose. Here’s what changed
articles.summary: The Giants have thrived in one-score games.
articles.body:
Since Giants tight end Chris Manhertz entered the NFL in 2015, he has seen plenty of different coaching styles while playing for six franchises.

He knows the best coaches in this league — like John Harbaugh — constantly emphasize late-game situations during practice. That is why the Giants have thrived in those settings this year under Harbaugh.

Manhertz loves that Harbaugh leans into practice scenarios "that put a little stress on us, so that we're accustomed to it," he told NJ.com.

That approach is paying off in a big way.

"Once the game time comes, we've seen it before," Manhertz said. "It gives us a boost of confidence that no matter what happens throughout these games, we have the ability to finish.

"It gives us confidence that we can pull ourselves out of anything, if we do what we're supposed to do. When certain things happen, no matter what, we don't blink — because we know that we have the ability to finish."

So much of thriving in the NFL comes down to that — finishing games.

It's not just that the Giants are 5-2-1 and securely alone atop the NFC East heading into Thursday night's home game against the Commanders.

It's not just that they are 4-1-1 without their starting quarterback, Jaxson Dart, who was supposed to ascend to face-of-the-franchise status this season.

No, this has been the singular magical stat for Harbaugh's remarkable, resilient first season: Excluding their 27-27 tie in Washington in Week 5, these Giants are 4-1 in one-score games (decided by eight points or fewer).

They beat Dallas by eight in Week 1, Tennessee by five in Week 3, Houston by six in overtime in Week 7 and Philadelphia by eight in Week 9. Plus, their 12-point win over Arizona in Week 4 would've been a six-point victory if not for a last-second pick-six.

Bottom line: They are thriving in tense, late-game situations — spots they wilted in last season under Brian Daboll's staff.

Yes, this year's Giants have lost by seven to the Saints (and 22 to the Rams after Dart's season-ending knee injury). But the New Orleans game was essentially a blowout loss that replacement quarterback J.J. McCarthy made close at the end, earning himself the starting job for the Houston trip.

So all five of the Giants' wins have come via strong play in the final moments, with four officially counting as one-score victories.

The past two years, the Giants went 7-27 overall — including 2-15 in one-score games (1-8 and then 1-7). That's the difference competent coaching makes.

"It's more from top to bottom being on the same accord," safety Jason Pinnock told NJ.com, as he pondered how things have changed in East Rutherford.

Pinnock was with Daboll from 2022-24, before spending last season with a much better head coach — the 49ers' Kyle Shanahan.

"Kyle is big on that, too," Pinnock said of the emphasis on working late-game situations during practice.

Shanahan, like Harbaugh, is an accomplished coach — an obvious statement that was pointed out to Pinnock. He nodded in agreement.

"So we're seeing the correlation here," he said. "Just being situationally aware. You've got to know clock, timeouts, just flow of the game."

During practice, Harbaugh goes through "any situation you could think of," Manhertz said. It's everything from the end of the first half to the end of a game to four-minute scenarios and two-minute drills. Harbaugh also hammers long-drive simulations, with the Giants down, say, a touchdown or a field goal.

"This coaching staff probably reps it a bit more," Manhertz said, comparing Harbaugh's approach to previous coaches he has played for. "Once you practice it and you go through multiple situations in games where it happens — and you come out on the good side of it — it gives you confidence to do it again."

articles.title: Cam Skattebo on Giants’ failed Jonathan Taylor pursuit: ‘You’ve seen what I can do’
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor did not get traded.
articles.body:
So much for Jonathan Taylor replacing Cam Skattebo as the Giants ' No. 1 running back.

Taylor is staying with the Colts, who decided to not deal him to the Giants (or anyone else) ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.

The Giants ultimately wound up doing nothing at the deadline, as prices rose across the NFL — something John Harbaugh, the team's coach and football czar, acknowledged Tuesday as the deadline approached.

"You don't want to make a bad deal," Harbaugh said. "You make a bad deal, that doesn't make you better. That makes you worse. Sometimes, the best deal is the deal that you don't make.

"We're willing to pay a price to make our team better. But it's got to be something that really makes our team better. It's got to be worth it. I would want a player that we love."

Harbaugh — who wants a sure-thing No. 1 back — yanked his Taylor offer of a second- and a fifth-round draft pick. He didn't love Taylor enough to offer more.

Taylor, a South Jersey high school legend, won't get his homecoming — though he could still be traded in the offseason, since he is under contract through 2028.

In the Giants' locker room Tuesday, Skattebo reacted to Taylor not being traded.

"You've seen what I can do," he said. "When I come out and I'm ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that."

He said he understood why Giants fans ­— who lionized him during his encouraging rookie year last season — wanted Taylor. But Skattebo, who is entering just his 16th NFL game, also expressed confidence in himself.

"I would be skeptical, too, if my running back was going for 60 yards a game and not really exploding out," he said. "But I'm still getting comfortable, man. This is like my 13th game in the league.

"I'm not even through a full football season yet. I'm still learning how to play football in this league. You obviously can see I'm getting more comfortable as I play the game."

As for the Taylor trade talks, Skattebo said, "Whether they were thinking about it or not, it doesn't bother me. I know I'm here, I'm healthy and I'm ready to play football. That's it."

(The Giants — led by Harbaugh — absolutely were thinking seriously about trading for Taylor. It just didn't work out, since the Colts wanted more.)

So what does Skattebo think about retaining his No. 1 back job?

"I've been that guy," he said. "Obviously, we had that one-week hiccup where I got in trouble [and got benched against the Saints]. That was it. I came back that next week and handled business. They know what I'm capable of. They know what I can do."

Skattebo is coming off last season's serious ankle injury. He recently said he was still working his way back from that. So where is he now?

"The ankle injury is the ankle injury," he said. "You deal with it for the next 10 years. It's something that's going to always be there. It's something that you have scars in your mental from. But once you do the rehab and you're continuously working on it, that's the big key.

"Probably the last three to four games, that's when I've really started to feel more comfortable and the ankle has really not given me any issues at all. I've been able to go into the games feeling 100% me."

Now, with nine games left in Harbaugh's magical first season, the Taylor-less Giants need Skattebo at his best.

The Giants are 5-2-1 and in first place in the NFC East entering Thursday night's home game against the Commanders. Harbaugh's team just won in Philadelphia for the first time since 2013, but Skattebo missed that game with a hamstring injury he suffered in the pre-bye week win at Houston.

Skattebo is expected to be ready for Thursday. He was close to being able to play at the Eagles. Against the Commanders, he will try to build on his strong showing in Houston, where he ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown during a thrilling overtime victory.

After Skattebo ran for 81 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 against Dallas, his production declined over the next four games, as he struggled with fumbling and scored zero touchdowns.

He ran for just 36, 60, 58 and 59 yards in those games. Then he was benched for the loss to the Saints, right before the Houston trip.

Skattebo did have 100 total yards in Week 3 against the Titans (because he posted 40 receiving yards that day). But overall, the Giants were not getting enough from their rushing attack prior to the Houston game.

During their 19-11 win at the Eagles, they needed to rely on Devin Singletary as their No. 1 back. (Tyrone Tracy, the No. 2 back, is on injured reserve with a hamstring issue.) The Giants managed 80 yards on 31 rushes in Philadelphia. Singletary had just 31 yards on 21 carries.

With Skattebo back in the mix — and Taylor staying in Indianapolis — can the Giants' rushing game get back on track against the Commanders?

articles.title: Chargers vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 10 Monday Night Football
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 and running out of opportunities to salvage their season. Fortunately, Monday night’s matchup against the Baltimore Ravens c...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 and running out of opportunities to salvage their season. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column.

Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns.

Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut

Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston.

Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore.

I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track.

Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team

This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable.

Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards.

The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver.

In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story.

Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season

The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do.

Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9.

There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches.

Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance.

Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play.

This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory.

Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage.

articles.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
articles.summary: The quarterback has been in concussion protocol since being injured Sept. 26 at USC.
articles.body:
Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night.

"I'm not anticipating him being back this season," Lanning said.

"Really got clarity for us this past week, for him," Lanning added. "And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it's not really up to Dante. It's not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he's able to do things for us, but that's not always the case in the game."

Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover.

"That hasn't changed," Lanning said. "Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that's not gonna happen."

Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team.

"He's still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better," Lanning said.

The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol.

Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn't know if he'd return this season and was taking it "one day at a time."

He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt.

Saturday's loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday.

Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas.

Moore was injured on Sept. 26 at USC while sliding to end a 10-yard run to the USC 13-yard line. As Moore began to slide, Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II hit him in the head with his shoulder.

Moore was taken off the field in a cart and loaded into an ambulance.

Following Moore's injury, Raiola entered the game and led the Ducks to a 41-27 win.

Moore entered the concussion protocol but returned to practice the following bye week.

Speculation was that Moore would return once he cleared the protocols. But each subsequent availability report listed Moore as out.

On Oct. 10, Oregon lost 17-15 to UCLA, with Raiola struggling through three quarters before being replaced in the fourth quarter by Thomas.

Thomas started the following week against Nebraska, but he played poorly before Raiola entered the game in the fourth quarter and led the Ducks to a 17-14 comeback win.

Oregon's realistic national playoff hopes remained alive at 4-2 — until the loss to Illinois.

At 4-3, the Ducks must win their final five games to reach 9-3 and hope enough playoff contenders finish with three losses so the Ducks can receive a berth.

If Moore enters the 2027 NFL Draft, his announcement will end his brief Ducks career, during which he led the program to one of its best seasons.

Lanning said he wasn't sure what Moore's plans were after this season.

"That's not fair for me to say or speculate," Lanning said. "Obviously, he'll have a decision again at the end of the season and what that looks like. I think we all can acknowledge that Dante is a great player and he will get an opportunity to get drafted. But what that looks like in the future, I think that's a decision for a later date. I don't know where his mind is at on that. We haven't had a conversation. That's not where my focus is at. I don't think that's where his focus is at right now. There's a reason you get time to make that decision later on."

Moore committed to Oregon in the summer of 2022. Later, he flipped to UCLA in December of 2022 rather than back up Ducks quarterback Bo Nix in 2023.

That summer, Moore learned that his mother had been diagnosed with cancer, adding to the pressure he was feeling while trying to perform as a highly touted freshman.

Moore had a rough freshman season at UCLA. His midseason struggles led Chip Kelly to bench Moore.

Following the season, Moore entered the transfer portal and committed to the Ducks in December 2023.

Moore transferred to Oregon to develop while backing up the team's new starter, Oklahoma transfer Dillon Gabriel.

That plan paid off in 2025. Moore passed for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while leading the Ducks to a 13-2 record and the playoff semifinals, where they lost to eventual national champion Indiana.

Moore, a projected first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, returned to Oregon for his senior season to keep improving with a team that returned eight defensive starters and was expected to contend for a national championship.

Oregon entered the season ranked No. 2 — the highest preseason ranking in program history — and defeated Boise State, 34-27, in the opener.

Moore passed for a career-high 378 yards with three touchdown passes.

The season began to unravel the following week when the heavily favored Ducks lost 39-31 at Oklahoma State.

The following week, Oregon won 84-0 over Portland State. Next came the USC game.

The Ducks, who host No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1), could continue to start Raiola or turn to former four-star recruit Akili Smith Jr.

Chances are, Lanning will go with whichever quarterback he believes can win games.

In the offseason, Oregon is expected to seek a quarterback in the transfer portal. With high expectations at Oregon, Lanning likely won't bank on Raiola or Smith as the starter in 2027.

articles.title: NFL odds, betting, storylines: 3 underdogs to back in Week 10
articles.summary: Let's look at three spots where some 'dogs are in position to bark in Week 10.
articles.body:
Sometimes, the truth hurts. This is one of those times: I misfired on both of my NFL underdog recommendations in Week 9.

Then again, virtually everyone who backed an NFL underdog in Week 9 misfired.

In what proved to be the most lopsided slate of the season to date, favorites last week went 14-1 SU and 11-3-1 ATS.

Following such a beatdown, underdog bettors are left to choose one of two paths: press pause and regroup, or press on and recoup. I'm taking the latter route.

Here are my three NFL underdog best bets for Week 10.

Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons

I acknowledge that the 2026 Atlanta Falcons have been the leading cause of ulcers for NFL bettors.

One week, the Falcons are getting crushed 34-3 by the Panthers at home. Then they're destroying the Packers and Saints in consecutive road games by a combined score of 80-38.

The next week, they're blowing a fourth-quarter lead to the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens and losing in overtime (again at home). Two weeks later, they're handing the 49ers their first loss, while dropping 29 points on one of the NFL's best defenses — promptly followed by two complete duds (a 16-0 loss at Tampa Bay and a 34-17 no-show against the Bengals in Madrid).

So why get involved with a clearly schizophrenic squad? One that has dropped seven straight games to AFC opponents and is now facing the 6-2 Chiefs, who hail from — spoiler alert — the AFC?

Well, for starters, the point spread in this contest is a head-scratcher — just as the 49ers-Falcons point spread was a head-scratcher.

Three weeks ago, San Francisco was 6-0 while Atlanta was coming off back-to-back, near-identical home losses to the Ravens (30-23) and Bears (31-23). Yet the Niners took the field in Atlanta as a scant 2.5-point favorite and lost 29-20.

The oddsmakers were telling us something with that line. And they're doing so again here. Think about it: The Falcons are coming off two losses by a collective score of 50-17. Also, since the calendar flipped to November, they've gone from Atlanta to Tampa Bay to Madrid to Atlanta. So why is this number so short?

I think it's because Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes isn't 100%. He suffered what looked to be an elbow injury in the first half against the Jets last week but played through it. Even healthy, Mahomes has struggled to push the ball down the field. In the past three games, no K.C. wideout has eclipsed 53 receiving yards.

It's also worth noting that only four of the Chiefs victories have been convincing: 31-10 over Denver in the opener, 24-10 at Miami, 22-6 over the Chargers and 35-12 over the Jets. The Broncos avenged their loss to the Chiefs two weeks ago; the latter three teams have a combined 3-22 record.

If the Falcons have done one thing consistently this season it's showing up when few expect them to. I'm banking on that happening again Sunday afternoon.

Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5) vs. Tennessee Titans

I'm not about to claim the Tennessee Titans — who are 7-35 since the 2024 season kicked off — have turned the corner. But they at least have shown a pulse over the last month.

Here's what Tennessee has done since opening the season with five straight losses:

A come-from-behind 26-20 victory at Indianapolis (outscoring the Colts 26-7 in the second half); a 27-24 home loss to Cleveland (a game the Titans led 14-0 and tied up with 58 seconds to play); and a 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati (the Bengals were 13.5-point favorites, the biggest spread in the NFL this season).

Much-maligned Titans quarterback Cam Ward threw for 304 yards in Cincinnati (besting his previous career high by 39 yards), and the offense produced a season-high 440 yards (after posting a season-high 322 yards against Cleveland the previous week).

Obviously — as Tennessee is well aware — this week's opponent is no joke. The Jaguars are 6-2. They have the No. 2-ranked scoring defense (15.4 points per game) and the No. 4-ranked scoring offense (28.6 ppg). And they just posted two victories over the Colts and Ravens by the combined score of 75-17 (hence their NFL-best plus-108 point differential, which is 29 points better than any other team).

Beyond all that, Jacksonville has taken seven of the last eight meetings against the Titans, winning and covering the last four in a row.

Again, though, Tennessee — which had a bye last week — has been feisty lately. Also, with their competitive overtime loss to the Bengals, the 2026 Titans improved to 4-1 ATS as an underdog of more than six points (including 2-0 ATS as a double-digit 'dog).

Finally, prior to last week's underdog blood bath, the biggest NFL favorite of the week had been just 4-4 SU and 2-6 ATS, with five straight non-covers. And for the season, double-digit favorites are just 2-5 ATS (and, to repeat, 0-2 ATS versus Tennessee).

Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5)

Are the Bengals — and particularly Joe Burrow — on fire right now? Yep. Have Burrow and his mates had this game circled on the calendar since suffering an upset loss at Pittsburgh 2½ months ago? No doubt about it.

But here's what else is true: That aforementioned near-loss at home to the Titans was just two weeks ago. More importantly, this is a terrible situational spot for Cincinnati, which faced Atlanta in Madrid last week while the Steelers enjoyed the week off.

Not only do the Steelers come into this Sunday Night Football game rested, but like Cincinnati, they're 6-2. And like Cincinnati, they're riding a four-game winning streak.

Unlike the Bengals, Pittsburgh covered the point spread in all four of those recent wins (Cincy is 2-1-1 ATS). And unlike the Bengals, Pittsburgh's defense is legit.

The Steelers surrender just 18 points and 305.6 yards per game, figures that respectively rank fourth and seventh in the NFL. And during the team's four-game heater, the defense has gotten increasingly stingier, allowing 22, 19, 10 and six points.

Granted, the four offenses Pittsburgh faced — Indianapolis, Tampa Bay, New Orleans and Cleveland — aren't in the same league as the Bengals. And, yes, back in Week 3 at Pittsburgh, the Bengals put up 27 points and 352 yards with Burrow posting excellent numbers (28-for-37 for 282 yards, three touchdowns, zero interceptions).

However, the Steelers put up 30 points and a still-season-high 411 yards that day. And old-man Aaron Rodgers (19-for-34, 292 yards, three TDs, one INT) was nearly as good as Burrow. Which brings me back to this point: The Bengals' defense remains untrustworthy (just ask Cam Ward).

Cincinnati very well may get its revenge in this one. But the Steelers will at least cover the spread — as they have in six of the last seven meetings in this rivalry.
